item.title: Ireland overcome Fiji to build up head of steam for South Africa clash
item.description: Ireland warmed up for a showdown with world champions South Africa by labouring to a 43-15 Nations Championship victory over Fiji in Dublin. The hosts had won all six previous Test matches between the sides but struggled for fluency and briefly trailed during an uncomfortable opening period at a subdued Aviva Stadium. Robert Baloucoune scored twice in the first half for Andy Farrell’s men after quick-fire tries from Fiji pair Josua Tuisova and Peceli Yato overturned Tommy O’Brien’s early opener. Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter, O’Brien and Nick Timoney went over in the second half as Ireland eventually pulled clear to keep alive their hopes of reaching the Nations Championship final. The result leaves Ireland level on 20 points with second-placed England in the northern hemisphere standings – a point below leaders France – ahead of next week’s mouthwatering clash with the Springboks. Head coach Farrell made seven personnel changes and two positional switches to his starting XV following last week’s convincing 42-12 win over Argentina, but insisted the selection was not experimental. Wing O’Brien, one of those recalled, crossed wide on the left to give Ireland an eighth-minute lead. Robert Baloucoune ran in two tries during the first half (Brian Lawless/PA) However, the hosts’ early promise faded after Jamison Gibson-Park had a try ruled out on review due to a knock-on. Fiji centre Tuisova powered over following a line-out maul before Jiuta Wainiqolo burst through a weak Irish defence to tee up captain Yato to put the visitors ahead. Boos rang around the ground when referee Angus Gardner ruled Ireland number eight Timoney had been held up on the line. Baloucoune then crossed twice in quick succession on the right, either side of a disallowed try for Fiji prop Luke Tagi, to restore order. Ronan Kelleher kickstarted Ireland’s second-half scoring (Brian Lawless/PA) But Ireland ended an underwhelming opening period with a slender 17-15 lead as Fiji fly-half Ben Volavola slotted a penalty after home captain Tadhg Beirne was sin-binned. Hooker Kelleher dived over at the start of the second half before O’Brien had to be alert to deny Volavola a breakaway try after he had charged down Sam Prendergast’s attempted clearance. Pop star Niall Horan was among the Lansdowne Road crowd and the scrappy contest gradually started to go in one direction. Nick Timoney wrapped up the victory for Ireland (Brian Lawless/PA) James McNabney’s Ireland debut from the bench lasted a matter of minutes after he was flattened by a swinging arm which resulted in a yellow card for Fiji’s replacement prop Inoke Ravuiwasa. Loosehead prop Porter bulldozed over following that incident before wing O’Brien’s 10th try in as many Tests increased the home side’s advantage further. Timoney completed the scoring by stretching for the line late on, but Ireland have work to do if they are to upset South Africa in seven days’ time.

item.title: Three sentenced to death over Jordan church attack
item.description: A Jordian court on Sunday sentenced the three gunmen responsible for a terror attack on a church funeral procession in the village of Hammoud that killed nine and wounded others. The attack prompted retaliatory strikes on "terrorist organisations" in neighbouring Syria.

item.title: From travel troubles to turf shoes, Tulane overcomes unusual obstacles at Rice
item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 24: Makai Williams #42 of the Tulane Green Wave, Zach Dresch #47 of the Tulane Green Wave and Cayden Dees #58 of the Tulane Green Wave run on the field prior to a game against the UTSA Roadrunners at Yulman Stadium on October 24, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Playing on the road in college football is challenging enough. But for several programs in Week 11 of the 2026 season, getting to the stadium became a battle of its own. On Friday, Nov. 13, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide ground stop, disrupting air travel across the country. The stoppage was just the third nationwide ground stop of the 21st century, following the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks and a Jan. 11, 2023 system outage. The Tulane Green Wave were preparing to fly to Houston for their matchup against Rice when their travel plans came to an abrupt halt. With no clear timeline when flights would resume, Tulane pivoted to an alternative that wasn’t a feasible option for many other programs affected by the shutdown. The Green Wave decided to take a nearly six-hour bus ride to Houston. “I want to give a big shoutout to (Chief of Staff) Chris Hatcher and (Director of Football Operations) Rory Thornton,” Tulane head coach Will Hall said. “When we got stopped right there on the tarmac, the efficiency with which they were able to turn this thing around — also credit to our administration, David Harris our athletic director, Patrick Norton, Justin Schemmel, and everybody involved right there to make sure this team was taken care of the best it could.” Tulane’s busses stopped in Lake Charles for a driver change before continuing west on the six-hour trek. The Green Wave ultimately arrived at its Houston hotel past 2 a.m. on Saturday. During the early stages of the trip, Rice and the American Conference agreed to delay the kickoff time two-and-a-half hours, pushing it from 1 p.m. CT to 3:30 p.m. CT. “We ended up bussing over,” Hall said. “We had our normal hotel meetings at the facility. We ate at the facility, we bussed over, we got here about 2:30 in the morning. And thank the league and thank Rice for backing up the kick time a little bit to allow our guys to sleep a little longer. It wasn’t an easy turn of events, but it’s what we want. We know that hard times develop hard men and tough times develop tough men. That’s what we tell our young men, and I thought they handled it elitely. They didn’t in any way use it as an excuse. We knew we had to win this game together. We knew it was gonna take all three phases, and we did it.” Roughly 13 hours after arriving in Houston, Tulane kicked off at First Community Stadium. The Green Wave withstood a sluggish start and turned a 17-6 halftime deficit into a 20-17 victory. A second half shutout from the defense and a late offensive surge allowed the team to secure its second consecutive road win over Hall after a night of complicated travel. “

item.title: '£47m? Why not?' - Former Liverpool centre-back Dejan Lovren tells club to seal bargain permanent deal for Barcelona loanee Ronald Araujo
item.description: Crystal Palace FC v Liverpool - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Former Liverpool defender Dejan Lovren has urged the Reds to trigger their €55 million (£47m) purchase option for Barcelona loanee Ronald Araujo. The 27-year-old centre-back has quickly become a mainstay at Anfield since arriving on a season-long deal from the Catalan giants in August. Uruguayan defender impresses on loan Lovren believes Anfield chiefs should waste no time tying down Araujo beyond June 30, 2027 following his seamless transition to English football. Since completing his temporary switch in the summer, the Uruguay international has featured in all 10 of the Merseysiders' opening Premier League matches, starting eight of them. His parent club still hold the defender under contract at Camp Nou until June 2031 . Former centre-back praises physical attributes Having registered 185 appearances and eight goals across all competitions during a six-year spell on Merseyside between 2014 and 2020 before departing for Russian outfit Zenit Saint Petersburg, the Croatian knows what is required at the heart of the backline. Across his English top-flight career, he tallied 162 outings and seven goals - combining 31 games and two strikes at former club Southampton with 131 matches and five goals for the Reds. Speaking to Tribal Football , Lovren explained why the newcomer thrives in England: "I believe the Premier League suits Ronald Araujo more than the Spanish league. Because he is a physically dominant guy, it suits him perfectly. "I believe he will only improve and, I don't know, maybe in the future he can agree to stay permanently. In the Premier League, Liverpool won't be his only option, but Liverpool are smart enough to consider their options, he's quite young at 27. So why not keep him if he's doing so well?" Purchase clause offers bargain value With rival top-flight clubs likely to monitor the centre-half's availability if he returns to Spain next summer, the former Croatia international feels the reported buyout fee represents an opportunity too good for his old employers to ignore. Pressing the hierarchy to make the arrangement permanent, Lovren added: "£47m? Why not? In the near future, he will probably cost £80m, so why not take him at this price and make him an even bigger and better player along the way? He's at a perfect age. He has a good five to six years at the top football level to play. So why not?" Fierce rivals visit Anfield next Addressing his long-term plans recently, Araujo insisted it remains "too early" to decide where he will play his football next season. For now, the defender is focused on helping fourth-placed Liverpool build on their 18-point haul from their opening 10 league outings. Once the international break concludes, the Reds return to top-flight action at Anfield against fierce rivals Manchester United in Matchday 11 on Sunday, November 22.

item.title: 'I still need to improve defensively!' – France surprise package Lucas Da Cunha opens up on Zinedine Zidane's tactical shift
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-FRA-TRAINING - AFP France midfielder Lucas Da Cunha has admitted he still needs to improve his defensive work after being deployed in a holding role by Zinedine Zidane. The Como captain discussed his rapid international rise ahead of Les Bleus' crucial UEFA Nations League fixture against Turkey. Lucas Da Cunha embraces surprising France role Como captain Lucas Da Cunha has quickly established himself as a surprise revelation under France coach Zinedine Zidane. Installed in a deep defensive midfield role, the 25-year-old has caught the eye during Les Bleus' UEFA Nations League campaign. Following a narrow defeat to Italy, Zidane's side are gearing up to face Turkey in Bordeaux. Da Cunha is expected to feature heavily as France look to secure qualification. Adapting to a demanding defensive midfield position Traditionally deployed further forward at club level under Cesc Fabregas, Da Cunha admitted that anchoring the French midfield requires a completely different physical and tactical approach . "It's true that I have a different role at Como, where I play further forward. Here, I'm in front of the defense, I don't have to push forward as much as at club level, but I like both positions," Da Cunha explained. "This holding midfield role is new to me; it requires a lot of defensive work, and physically I'm not a monster. I have to win back possession, and I can still improve defensively." Cesc Fabregas and Zinedine Zidane's influence Da Cunha credited his development at club level under Fabregas with preparing him for the tactical demands of international football. Since moving to Italy, the former Rennes youngster has successfully transformed from a winger into a complete central midfielder. The Como skipper also highlighted the personal support he received from Zidane after receiving his maiden senior call-up in September. "He made me feel that I wasn't there for nothing, he talked to me a lot to get to know me, our relationship is very good," Da Cunha revealed. Speaking about captain Kylian Mbappe ahead of the Turkey clash, the midfielder added: "He's in good form and we can feel he's fully committed to us. Like all of us, he's confident before the match." Preparing for high-stakes clash against Turkey France enter Sunday evening's encounter at the Stade Atlantique knowing that victory is essential to bounce back from their San Siro setback and secure quarter-final qualification. While Zidane remains calm following their first defeat in charge, insisting that the squad is entirely focused and not worried, the pressure is on Les Bleus to deliver. With Da Cunha anchoring the midfield and Mbappe leading the attack, France are primed to finish their group stage campaign on a high note.

item.title: “He Should Never Play Another Game for USC”: Trojans Fans Sick of Jayden Maiava After 3 INT Performance in 27–13 Loss vs. Indiana
item.description: Southern California Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava. © IMAGN USC Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava had a disappointing outing in the 27-13 loss against the Indiana Hoosiers. He threw three interceptions, including two in the fourth quarter that helped No. 9 Indiana secure the victory. Maiava completed 26 of 42 passes for 311 yards and one touchdown. In the three losses USC has suffered this season, Maiava has thrown for 894 yards with four TDs against six interceptions, struggling in tougher matchups. Fans shared their opinions on Maiava after USC’s loss against Indiana. “Jayden Maiava should never play another game for USC,” one fan wrote. USC QB Jayden Maiava Accepts His Mistakes in Indiana Loss Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava started well in the first half against Indiana, completing 14 of 16 passes for 145 yards, one touchdown and one interception. The game was tied at 10 entering halftime. However, Maiava struggled in the second half. With USC trailing 20-13 in the fourth quarter, linebacker Isaiah Jones picked off Maiava inside Indiana’s five-yard line. Maiava was then intercepted by Jamari Sharpe in the fourth quarter to end any comeback hopes for USC. His first interception came in the second quarter to Indiana defensive back Preston Zachman, setting up a 21-yard field goal for the Hoosiers. After the loss, Maiava acknowledged he could have done better. “Just got to play better at the quarterback position. Trust it and be able to flush it,” Maiava said via SI . “It was a great defense. We got a really great offense as well. Just got to play better at the quarterback position.” The defeat is USC’s third of the season, denting its chances for a spot in the 12-team College Football Playoff field. item.title: England are favourites against All Blacks, and fearless Wales are an inspiration
item.description: [BBC] In his latest BBC Sport column, England World Cup winner Matt Dawson reflects on Steve Borthwick's side's emphatic 78-15 thrashing of Japan and looks ahead to the match against New Zealand next weekend. I would love to see the England players absolutely bombarded with the favourites tag before their meeting with New Zealand next week. Perhaps even over-egg it a little bit - I want to see how this side handles it. At the end of the day, beating New Zealand or South Africa will likely be a requirement if you want to win a Rugby World Cup. Are England really favourites? Yes, I genuinely believe they are. While victories over Australia and Japan have been encouraging, it was Wales' epic win over the All Blacks on Saturday that has given me real faith that this England side is good enough to compete at the highest level. The key question is whether they can play as they have done over the last two weeks while carrying the favourites tag. England are playing a better style of rugby than New Zealand. I thought the All Blacks' attack, particularly in the second half in Cardiff, was incredibly one-dimensional. That is nothing for England to be afraid of as their own attack has been very slick this campaign. New Zealand aren't going to fix those issues in a week, and England should be capable of soaking up that style of attack defensively. Of course, the All Blacks were missing some frontline players, including Cam Roigard, Damian McKenzie, Will Jordan and Jordie Barrett. However, what I saw during the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series was the Springboks beginning to work out that style of play after losing the first Test. They went on to win the next three Tests in a row. Two Tests to turn England into World Cup contenders Having beaten the All Blacks last year, I don't want England to approach this home fixture with an underdog mentality. This side needs to get used to being a contender. The next few weeks could prove crucial in determining whether they are genuine challengers at next year's World Cup. An undefeated autumn, regardless of whether they finish top of the northern hemisphere standings in the Nations Championship, would elevate England to contenders for the Six Nations. Two weeks ago, England would have been delighted to find themselves in this position. Now, the reward could be two massive Tests against the very best. They are not at the level of France or South Africa yet. I think those two sides, particularly after Friday's Test match, are still a little bit ahead of everybody else. However, England have a good chance of facing New Zealand back-to-back over the next two weeks. What an unbelievable opportunity that would be and what a feather in the cap it would represent for this team. It would not only give the players belief in what they are capable of achieving, but also send a message to the rest of the world that they can beat New Zealand and potentially follow that up with another victory over the All Blacks or South Africa. item.title: 3 takeaways from No. 2 Utah’s thrilling victory over No. 23 Arizona
item.description: Arizona wide receiver Isaiah Mizell (17) leaps for a first down against Utah in the first half of an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, in Tucson, Ariz. | Rick Scuteri, Associated Press In a game that saw seven lead changes throughout, the No. 2 Utah Utes overcame a delayed flight, an almost entirely unavailable Wayshawn Parker and a slow start to down Noah Fifita and the No. 23 Arizona Wildcats in an absolute thriller, 40-39 on the road Saturday. The Utes trailed 14-3 before scoring the game’s next 14 points to go up 17-14. From there, the teams went back and forth, exchanging leads as they both showcased their offensive explosiveness led by their respective quarterbacks. Here are three keys that led to Utah’s win. Utah played just well enough to overcome three turnovers A week ago against BYU, the Utes created havoc for rival quarterback Bear Bachmeier as he threw four interceptions, two of which were thrown from inside the 10 when the Cougars were close to scoring. This week it was the other way around. Devon Dampier had a poor pitch that did not find his running back’s hands, and after falling to the ground, found the arms of an Arizona lineman ready to pounce on the first play of the second half, one that Arizona also capitalized on for six points. Dampier also threw an interception in the third quarter that was picked by Arizona’s Jay’Vion Cole at the 1-yard line, where Fifita put together a 99-yard drive to retake the lead. Utah punt returner Mana Carvalho also muffed a punt that gave the ball right back to Arizona. However, the Ute defense held strong for a three-and-out to escape the situation with just giving up a field goal. Ultimately, despite costly mistakes, Dampier’s 204 passing yards and 100 rushing yards were enough to get the job done with assistance from Daniel Bray in the backfield. As the Utes have seen, momentum swings can be the difference in losing and winning. Fortunately for the Utes Saturday, the turnovers did not cost them the game, but head coach Morgan Scalley will surely make ball security a point of emphasis in the week ahead as the Utes look to the TCU Horned Frogs. item.title: Dana White admits he was wrong about Josh Hokit after UFC 334: 'Stock went up with me'
item.description: Josh Hokit may not have won Saturday night at UFC 334, but he still delivered a memorable performance in his first UFC main event . Heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane successfully defended his title with a unanimous decision win over Hokit at New York’s Madison Square Garden, a bout that earned Fight of the Night honors and a $100,000 performance bonus for each man. Although the result marked Hokit's first career defeat in 11 pro fights, UFC CEO Dana White couldn't have been more impressed with the outspoken contender. "It was an incredible fight," White said backstage at the UFC 334 post-fight press conference. "The pace he set was insane, and I think it was freaking everybody out — this smaller guy, the way he was just coming at [Gane]. But even if you look at the significant strikes, they were doubling every round. The total punch stats were massive, too. "If you see the score of the fight, they had it two-to-two going into the last round. I didn't see it that way, but it doesn't tell the story of the fight either. You have to see the fight to believe it." Hokit, 28, has experienced a meteoric rise since joining the promotion a year ago. In that time, White has openly admitted a distaste for how the former NFL player has presented himself with his character work and controversial comments, most notably when Hokit insulted former First Lady Michelle Obama on the White House’s South Lawn . Ciryl Gane and Josh Hokit had an all-out war of attrition Saturday at UFC 334. Caleb Bowlin via Getty Images White said he even scored Saturday’s fight four rounds to one in favor of Gane — yet he still believes the fight went perfectly for Hokit, despite a loss being the official result. "What he did was he went in there, and if you really think about going into this fight: How does Josh Hokit win this fight?" White said. "Ciryl Gane moves like a middleweight. He turned it into a street fight from the second the bell rang in the first round. Literally, he didn't win, but he fought the perfect fight. What other way could he possibly fight Ciryl Gane than the way that he did? "My thing was, after the first round, holy s*** — if he can keep this pace for five rounds, Gane's in big trouble. Too big, carries too much muscle and blah, blah, blah. But actually, Gane looked his best in the fourth and fifth rounds. "There's no doubt that Hokit's stock goes up. Even with me," White continued. "I thought this guy was a big-mouth goofball and I hated his schtick and the whole thing. I respect the s*** out of that guy [now]. He is the real deal. Stock went up with me." Hokit beat two longtime heavyweight contenders, Curtis Blaydes and Derrick Lewis , to earn his title shot. The latter came on the big stage that was UFC Freedom 250 at the White House in June. Before and after that fight, it seemed more likely Hokit would face former two-division champion Alex Pereira than earn a title shot, especially since Pereira lost to Gane that same night in the nation’s capital. item.title: 'Of course it is annoying!' – Zinedine Zidane blasts media reports over his relationship with Kylian Mbappe
item.description: FBL-EUR-NATIONS-FRA-TRAINING - AFP France head coach Zinedine Zidane has strongly denied any friction between himself and captain Kylian Mbappe. Speaking ahead of their crucial UEFA Nations League fixture against Turkey, Zidane branded media speculation regarding their relationship as entirely false and annoying. Zidane hits back at Mbappe rift rumours France head coach Zinedine Zidane has firmly put to bed any talk of a strained relationship with national team captain Kylian Mbappe. Speaking ahead of Sunday's crucial UEFA Nations League clash against Turkey in Bordeaux, Zidane addressed media speculation head-on . With Les Bleus needing a victory to secure qualification on a high note, the manager stressed that unity within the camp remains absolute. 'The relationship is perfectly fine' Press conference inquiries quickly turned to rumoured friction between the manager and his star striker ahead of the Stade Atlantique fixture. With an impassive expression, Zidane made it clear that stories of a fallout are completely wide of the mark. "I don't quite understand what's being written," Zidane stated firmly. "I'm not going to get into the debate; the relationship is perfect. For the player as well as for me. I can't stop what's being said." When pressed on whether the ongoing reports had frustrated him, the former midfielder admitted that the speculation is wearing thin. "Yes, the things that come back to me, of course, are quite annoying," he added. Tactical plans and squad updates for Turkey On the pitch, Zidane confirmed that Mbappe will start in his preferred position, leading a 4-3-3 attacking trident as France look to bounce back from a 3-1 defeat against Italy. "Of course it changes everything, we'd rather have him with us than not have him," Zidane noted regarding his talisman. Elsewhere in camp, young forward Désiré Doué trained despite struggling with an unstable tooth following an elbow from Davide Frattesi. Meanwhile, players like Michael Olise and Bradley Barcola are tipped to support Mbappe in attack, with defensive changes expected as Les Bleus chase victory. All eyes on Bordeaux showdown with Turkey Sunday evening's encounter at the Stade Atlantique carries massive significance as Les Bleus aim to bounce back and seal their qualification status in style. Zidane's men know that a strong performance against the Turks will banish memories of their San Siro setback. With the squad fully focused and their captain primed to lead the line, France are ready to deliver a statement display in their final group outing.

item.title: “Tennessee Broke This Man’s Soul”: Fans React to Mike Elko “Begging for His Job” With His “Utter Apology” After Texas A&M’s Loss
item.description: Texas A&M Aggies head coach Mike Elko during warm ups before Auburn Tigers take on Texas A&M Aggies at Jordan-Hare Stadium in Auburn, Ala., on Saturday, Nov. 23, 2024. Mike Elko has not been a name that many will hear about this season, but he made himself known on Saturday – for the wrong reasons. Shortly after Texas A&M suffered a 7-22 home drubbing against Tennessee, the Aggies’ head coach opened his post-game presser with this statement: “Utter apology with everything that I have to everybody that supports this program. Thank you for turning out; you deserve so much better. Give me a chance & we will get this fixed and put a much better product on the field.” His attempt at contrition, unfortunately, was met with derision and condemnation from fans: The game was notable for some underwhelming quarterback performances. For Texas A&M, Marcel Reed completed only nine of 22 attempts for 71 yards and was intercepted once, while Brady Hart added another pick. The team’s only touchdown came on a KJ Edwards run. George MacIntyre, meanwhile, had just 109 yards for Tennessee before exiting in the third quarter with a knee injury, but he set up two field goals for Cooper Ranvier. After taking over, Faizon Brandon threw a touchdown pass to DeSaahn Brame and then set up three more field goals. Texas A&M HC Mike Elko discusses Aggies’ offensive woes vs. Tennessee All told, Mike Elko had just one word to describe how Texas A&M’s offense fared on Saturday: “Pathetic.” He continued: “The wind played a big role,” explained Elko. “The (pass) rush played a bigger role. Our inability to give (Marcel Reed) any time to see anything — they’re very multiple on defense — so the pressure created a massive challenge trying to do anything.” The Aggies will visit Oklahoma next week. Kickoff is at 11 a.m. CT. item.title: Coco Gauff’s Ex-Coach Urges Aryna Sabalenka to Make Major Changes To Her Team After WTA Finals Heartbreak: “Hard Questions to Figure Out”
item.description: Aug 8, 2026; Toronto, Ontario, Canada; Aryna Sabalenka reacts after missing a point against Ekaterina Alexandrova (not pictured) during the fourth round at the National Bank Open at Sobeys Stadium. © John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images Coco Gauff’s former coach Brad Gilbert weighed in on Aryna Sabalenka’s WTA Finals disappointment, urging the Belarusian to make changes to her coaching team. The Belarusian stopped working with Max Mirnyi ahead of the WTA Finals, but is still working with head coach Anton Dubrov and performance coach Jason Stacy. Sabalenka’s run at the WTA Finals ended after she lost two of her three round-robin matches. She failed to win a Grand Slam this season and did not lift a title since the Sunshine Double. Sabalenka was also surpassed by Elena Rybakina for the top spot in the world rankings. Noting Sabalenka’s lackluster run, Gilbert suggested she make changes to her team. He opined that if he were in Sabalenka’s place, he would have promoted Mirnyi as head coach. On the Big T podcast , Gilbert also suggested that she make changes to her serve and forehand. “I think the biggest thing for this off-season is going to be the serve, and I do feel all of a sudden the forehand, which I do think is her best shot, has been letting her down a lot. I think she might need some changes to her team. I heard she let Max Mirnyi go. I would have promoted him to head coach. She’s got some hard questions to figure out this off-season to start the year very positively because she’s played well Down Under (at the Australian Open) the last few years.” Sabalenka has won the Australian Open twice, in 2023 and 2024. Aryna Sabalenka apologizes after video of her comments to fans spreads online Aryna Sabalenka issued an apology after a video of her comments to fans surfaced online after her WTA Finals loss to Elina Svitolina. “I want to clarify something from my recent match that has been circulating online. My comment was not directed at Elina. I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment. That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone I offended. Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament.” Screenshot of Aryna Sabalenka’s Instagram story. Elina Svitolina, meanwhile, advanced to the final of the year-end event, where she will take on Mirra Andreeva. item.title: 2027: Inuwa Yahaya flags off APC campaign, targets 1m votes for Tinubu
item.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe BAJOGA, the headquarters of Funakaye Local Government Area of Gombe State, was the venue of the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign flag-off on Saturday, as Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya declared the state ready to support President Bola Tinubu and other candidates of the ruling party in the 2027 general elections. At the rally, which attracted party supporters and political stakeholders from across the state, Inuwa Yahaya said the APC was targeting at least one million votes for Tinubu, expressing confidence that the party would win all elective positions in Gombe. The event was attended by the Special Adviser to the President on Political and Other Matters, Hon. Ibrahim Kabir Masari; APC Deputy National Chairman (North), Hon. Ali Bukar Dalori; former governors, members of the National Assembly and other party chieftains. Addressing the gathering, the governor urged residents to assess the APC based on its performance in government, highlighting projects and programmes implemented by his administration and the Federal Government. He particularly commended Tinubu’s electricity sector reforms, saying they had created opportunities for state governments to participate in power generation, transmission and distribution. Inuwa Yahaya cited the one-megawatt solar power project commissioned in Talasse and ongoing four-megawatt power projects in Kaltungo, Kumo, Bajoga and Dukku as examples of the benefits of the reforms. He also listed the Kaltungo Snakebite Research Centre, Federal Orthopaedic Hospital in Billiri, Federal Medical Centre in Kumo and ongoing interventions at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe, among federal projects in the state. On transportation infrastructure, the governor identified the Akwanga-Jos-Bauchi-Gombe-Biu road corridor and the proposed railway development from Jos towards the North-East as projects expected to improve connectivity and economic activities in the region. He also highlighted the Ultramodern International Livestock Market, International Grains Market, Timberland Abattoir and Inland Dry Port as initiatives aimed at strengthening Gombe’s commercial activities, attracting investment and creating employment opportunities. The governor said his administration had constructed more than 1,100 kilometres of roads across the state, adding that the APC was seeking the electorate’s support based on its record in office. “We are not promising; we are asking you to rate us based on our deliverables. Development has been taken to every nook and cranny of the state,” he said. item.title: LSU’s Lane Kiffin Answers Tough Question About $91 Million Investment in Him
item.description: AUBURN, ALABAMA - OCTOBER 24: Head coach Lane Kiffin of the LSU Tigers looks on during the first half of an NCAA football game against the Auburn Tigers at Jordan Hare Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Auburn, Alabama. (Photo by Stew Milne/Getty Images) Getty BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 14: Head Coach Lane Kiffin of the Louisiana State Tigers and Head Coach Steve Sarkisian of the Texas Longhorns interact on the field after the game at Tiger Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) Getty The LSU Tigers spent big money when they went out and got Lane Kiffin. A first-year home run was never guaranteed, and building something new can involve trial and error regardless of the coach’s experience. Still, LSU wants results now, and a 6-4 record made a question about its investment entirely fair. After Saturday’s 22-21 loss to Texas, Kiffin faced that question during his postgame media session. The Tigers committed to a seven-year, $91 million contract when they hired him. Asked about the expectations surrounding his arrival, Kiffin gave an answer that started where it needed to: with accountability. “Fair question, and I get it,” Kiffin said in footage of the news conference provided by Mike Scarborough of TigerBait. “Underperformance.” Lane Kiffin Acknowledges LSU Needs More Wins That opening was the strongest part of his response. Kiffin did not dismiss the premise or suggest that close losses should satisfy people who expected more. He acknowledged the gap between what LSU hired him to do and what the Tigers have delivered. “It doesn’t matter if the game’s been close or they go down to the last whatever, six seconds,” Kiffin said. “I’m brought here to win, and we need to win more than that.” The Texas game made that point particularly painful. LSU had a two-score lead before the Longhorns rallied, leaving the Tigers to explain another result they had opportunities to prevent. Being competitive against a good opponent offers little comfort when the win was within reach. Getty BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA – NOVEMBER 14: Head Coach Lane Kiffin of the Louisiana State Tigers and Head Coach Steve Sarkisian of the Texas Longhorns interact on the field after the game at Tiger Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) Kiffin then addressed the longer view. He argued that establishing the roster he wants involves more than the results of one season. Importantly, he did not say that development makes the current losses acceptable. Kiffin Explains the Work Behind Building LSU’s Roster “Also, everything isn’t built for the first year when you come in somewhere,” Kiffin said. “I would tell you that if we were undefeated right now. You build things, and they take a little bit of time.” Kiffin said fans could see the difference just by watching Texas warm up. item.title: Manchester City Eyeing £35 Million-Rated Lens Goalkeeper Amid Gianluigi Donnarumma Struggles
item.description: Manchester City Eyeing £35 Million-Rated Lens Goalkeeper Amid Gianluigi Donnarumma Struggles Gianluigi Donnarumma has struggled in net for Manchester City of late. More Videos Gianluigi Donnarumma remains Enzo Maresca’s first-choice goalkeeper, but it has not been the most convincing start to the season for the Italian. A number of costly errors have placed his form under scrutiny, forcing Maresca to publicly back his No. 1 on more than one occasion and prompting some supporters to argue that their side needs more competition between the sticks. With Geronimo Rulli approaching 35 years of age, that competition would likely have to come from the transfer market - which is where a new name linked with Manchester City will raise eyebrows. It’s safe to assume that the club’s recruitment staff have continued to track the next generation of goalkeepers across Europe even after the signing of Donnarumma, and fresh rumours suggest the search has taken them to France. Trophy-winning Lens shotstopper being considered by Man City The name in question is RC Lens goalkeeper Robin Risser, who was part of France’s World Cup squad in the summer after a meteoric rise in senior football. According to Swiss outlet 4-4-2.ch , as relayed by Sports Mole , Manchester City are leading the chase for the 21-year-old and are considering an opening bid of around £26 million ahead of the summer window. Lens, however, are holding out for at least £35 million for a player contracted until June 2030. Risser was central to a superb 2025-26 campaign at Lens as they finished second in Ligue 1 and lifted the Coupe de France. That form earned him the UNFP Goalkeeper of the Year award and a place in the competition’s Team of the Year. The 6ft 4in Risser boasts a commanding aerial presence and composure on the ball, making him exactly the kind of profile that would suit Manchester City ’s build-up play. The sticking point is a sell-on clause inserted by Strasbourg, reported as 25 per cent of the total fee - or 25 per cent of the profit according to L’Équipe - meaning a significant chunk of any sale would be owed to his old club. Risser’s current season has admittedly been more difficult than the last, not least with a chastening 9-1 UEFA Champions League defeat at home to Como earlier this month. His standing at international level has held firm, though, with the youngster called up under both Didier Deschamps and new France boss Zinedine Zidane. That promise has not gone unnoticed elsewhere. Liverpool and Manchester United are reportedly both keeping tabs, as are Serie A pair Inter Milan and Juventus, while Newcastle United and Tottenham have shown interest in the past. No formal offers have been tabled as yet.

item.title: Declan Rice hopes to sign new Arsenal contract soon as talks continue over long-term deal
item.description: Declan Rice hopes to sign new Arsenal contract soon as talks continue over long-term deal Declan Rice has said that he hopes to sign a new contract with Arsenal 'soon'. Arsenal have been in talks with the England midfielder's representatives over a new deal in North London, as the Gunners look to secure the future of the 27-year-old. Rice has been an integral part of Arsenal's success since signing from West Ham in a club-record deal in 2023, and has been named the club's Player of the Season in each of the last two campaigns. The midfielder helped Arsenal to a drought-breaking Premier League title in 2025/26, alongside a first Champions League final in 20 years. He was also nominated for the Ballon d'Or for the third consecutive campaign. Arsenal are eager to agree a new long-term deal with Rice, after new contracts for Mikel Arteta and Bukayo Saka in recent months. Speaking ahead of England's fixture with Spain in the UEFA Nations League this evening, Rice said he's hopeful a new contract can be sorted in the near future. "I've been extremely lucky that I've managed to play at such a consistent level throughout my career," he said. "I'm a player that always sets myself targets, always pushes for more. I've always been stable in the clubs I'm at. New contract hopefully on the horizon soon. "I'm extremely lucky I'm at a club like Arsenal where the manager shows me so much trust, I've so many teammates who put so much energy and effort into me. I'm extremely lucky that I don't have to worry about that stuff. It makes playing football a lot easier."

item.title: Dominik Livakovic talks life in Barcelona, training and game-time under Flick
item.description: Dominik Livakovic talks life in Barcelona, training and game-time under Flick Dominik Livakovic was somewhat of a surprise signing for Barcelona when the club roped him in the summer for a fee of just €2 million. It was an investment made keeping in mind Wojciech Szczesny’s future, with Livakovic immediately being promoted as the main alternative to Joan Garcia. Currently on duty with the Croatian national team, Livakovic has opened up about his time at Barcelona so far, including his lack of game-time among other things. Livakovic on game-time at Barcelona Livakovic has won 84 caps for Croatia. (Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images) Livakovic was asked whether or not his lack of minutes at Barcelona affects his standing in the Croatian national team. “I play for Barcelona. I’m just a young man from Zadar, and I’m very proud of that. I’ve already kept goal for this great club. I train and wait for my chance, and I feel like I’m in good shape,” he said (h/t Diario SPORT ). Livakovic, who started in the recent game against England , went on to describe the training process at Barcelona, which he labelled tough. The goalkeeper added that he is waiting for his chance to impress. “Training at Barcelona really is very tough, because we’re talking about the best players in the world. It would be ideal to play in goal in every match, but I’m waiting patiently for my chance ,” he added. Livakovic has so far made only one appearance for Barcelona since joining the club in the summer. That lone appearance came against Sevilla earlier in the campaign. Livakovic on being awarded Fiery Heart trophy Livakovic is regarded highly in Croatian football. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) Meanwhile, it was a special day for Livakovic as he was awarded the Fiery Heart trophy for his selfless service to the Croatian national team. Speaking about the accolade, the goalkeeper said, “This award has made me very happy, because it comes from the fans who give football its passion and special emotions. “ “I truly care, from the bottom of my heart, about the national team’s success, and I’m happy that the fans recognized that and appreciated it in this way. “ Livakovic added that it’s an honour to follow in the footsteps of Croatian legends such as Ivan Perisic and Luka Modric, previous recipients of the award. “It’s wonderful to follow in the footsteps of Luka and Perišić, who won this award before me, and that alone shows its value. “I thank everyone who took part in the voting, and I extend a special thank-you to all the fans who continue to support us, whether things are going well or we’re going through tougher times,” he concluded.

item.title: ‘A Lot Of Negative Things Happened’ — Super Bowl-Winning HC Pushes Mike Vrabel’s Patriots To Clean Up Their Act
item.description: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. The New England Patriots have shown they can move the ball and put points on the board, but their recent performances have exposed a problem that keeps putting them in difficult positions. Falling behind early has forced Mike Vrabel’s team to spend too much time chasing games instead of controlling them. Super Bowl-winning coach Jon Gruden believes the Patriots need to address that habit before it costs them again. Jon Gruden Urges Mike Vrabel’s Patriots to Fix Their Slow Starts Gruden shared his assessment in a video on X, pointing out that New England’s overall offensive production has not been the problem. The former Tampa Bay Buccaneers coach, who led the team to a Super Bowl XXXVII victory, believes the Patriots must translate that production into better openings. “The Patriots’ offense averages 23.4 points per game. That’s 14th in the league. They’re eighth in total offense. It’s a credit to them,” Gruden said. “They average 369 yards a game, rank 10th in rushing and ninth in passing. But they have to resolve the slow starts. There’s nothing worse than a slow start.” He then highlighted how New England has fallen behind in recent games. Against Green Bay in Week 9, the Patriots allowed a 17-0 lead after a difficult opening stretch. Their previous two games followed a similar pattern, with Chicago taking an early 10-0 advantage and Miami leading 13-3 at halftime. The team ranks 16th in PFN NFL Defense Impact %20assigns,red%20zone%20and%20third%20downs.) with a 74.1 grade. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor “I mean, hell’s bells. Their first 15 plays of the game, a lot of negative things happened, and they fell behind 17-0 to the Packers,” Gruden said. “The week before that, they were down 13-3 to Miami at halftime. The week before that, they were down just like that, 10-0 to the Chicago Bears.” New England recovered to beat Miami 24-19, but its comeback efforts could not prevent losses to Chicago and Green Bay. The Packers handed New England a 45-27 defeat, scoring the most points any visiting team has managed against the Patriots at Gillette Stadium. Drake Maye threw an interception on his first pass and finished with 3 interceptions in all, bringing his season total to 11. Gruden believes the Patriots need to take control from the opening drive rather than rely on second-half rallies. “They have to start faster, get a lead, man, so they can dictate things,” he said. The criticism comes as New England tries to regain its form after a 14-3 season and a Super Bowl LX appearance in Vrabel’s first year. The Patriots are now 5-4 and sit second in the AFC East, with turnovers and penalties adding to their problems. Their next challenge is a Week 10 matchup against the 6-2 Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Rex Ryan’s Status for ‘Sunday NFL Countdown’ Revealed After Arrest
item.description: BEVERLY HILLS, CA - JULY 26: Former NFL coach & ESPN analyst Rex Ryan of 'ESPN's Sunday's NFL Countdown' speaks onstage during the ESPN portion of the 2017 Summer Television Critics Association Press Tour at The Beverly Hilton Hotel on July 26, 2017 in Beverly Hills, California. (Photo by Frederick M. Brown/Getty Images) Getty Former New York Jets and Buffalo Bills head coach Rex Ryan was in the news for the wrong reasons this week. After stepping away from coaching in 2016, Ryan joined ESPN as an NFL analyst, primarily appearing on “Sunday NFL Countdown.” However, he turned himself in to Nashville authorities early Wednesday morning after allegedly running over the feet of two pedestrians with his truck on Broadway Street. Ryan drove away but eventually stopped at a red light, where he got out and argued with the pedestrians. He then returned to his vehicle and left the scene. Authorities later identified his license plate and traced the truck’s registration to him. The former NFL coach now faces six misdemeanor counts: leaving the scene of an accident (2), failure to give information or render aid (2), and failure to obey a traffic control signal (2). Will Ryan Be on ESPN Sunday Morning? With Sunday morning approaching, a big question is whether Ryan will appear alongside the NFL Countdown crew, which consists of host Mike Greenberg, Alex Smith, Teddy Bruschi, Randy Moss and Adam Schefter. As of now, according to a statement from an ESPN spokesperson, Ryan will be on the show, and there is no expectation that he’ll address the matter. “As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown.” Ryan also usually appears on the morning show “Get Up” on Mondays following the NFL slate, so it’s likely he’ll be on air for each of the next two days. From an ESPN spokesperson on Rex Ryan: “As of now, Rex will appear as scheduled, including on Sunday NFL Countdown.” Would not expect Ryan to address the matter on air. — Richard Deitsch (@richarddeitsch) November 15, 2026 Ryan’s Time as Jets Head Coach While Ryan coached the Bills for two years, he was best known for his six seasons as the Jets’ head coach. The last time New York won a playoff game was in 2011, when Ryan was still coaching the team. He compiled a 46-50 regular-season record but went 4-2 in the postseason, including back-to-back trips to the AFC Championship Game. Those appearances came during his first two seasons with the organization, while the four years that followed didn’t go as planned. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Rex Ryan’s Status for ‘Sunday NFL Countdown’ Revealed After Arrest appeared first on HEAVY .

item.description: Tom Jordan David Brooks will be hoping his latest contribution for Wales can prove to be a turning point in what has been a frustrating start to the season at Bournemouth . The Cherries midfielder has found opportunities and consistent performances hard to come by in the early stages of the campaign, struggling to make the same impact that supporters have come to expect from him. However, finding the back of the net for his country and putting in an influential display off the bench could provide exactly the confidence boost he needs. International football can often offer players the opportunity to reset, rediscover their rhythm and remind everyone of their quality, and Brooks will be keen to bring that renewed belief back to the south coast. Bournemouth continue to face a demanding schedule so with plenty of opportunities still to come, this could be the moment for Brooksy to reignite his season and force his way back into the picture. The Cherries midfielder brought fresh energy and attacking intent to the Welsh side, capping his performance with a brilliantly taken goal. While the result was far from what Wales would have wanted, Brooks gave supporters something to cheer about and demonstrated the quality he still possesses. His contribution was recognised with Wales' Player of the Match award, a deserved accolade given the influence he had despite his time on the pitch being limited. For Brooks, it was an important personal moment and a timely reminder of what he can offer. Having struggled to make a consistent impact for Bournemouth this season, this could provide a valuable confidence boost ahead of returning to club action. item.title: IPL retention vs release vs trade: Explaining the difference ahead of Indian Premier League 2027 mini-auction
item.description: IPL retention vs release vs trade: Explaining the difference ahead of Indian Premier League 2027 mini-auction originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Three roster tools will shape every IPL franchise’s plans before the Goa mini-auction. A fresh salary cap figure and recent blockbuster swaps show how each option works. MI , PBKS , CSK and SRH have already used the trade route this month. MORE: IPL 2027 trade tracker: Complete list of all player and cash deals How do IPL retention, release, and player trades work? Complete guide ahead of the IPL 2027 mini-auction in Goa Retention, release and trade are the three words that dominate every IPL franchise’s conversation at this time of year, and each of them changes a squad and its spending power in a very different way. All teams must hand in their final retention and release lists by Tuesday, November 17. The BCCI moved the date back by two days from November 15 because of an India–New Zealand ODI clash, while the mini-auction itself stays on December 16 in Goa. The auction is due to be held at ITC Grand Goa. It will be the last mini-auction of the current cycle, with a mega auction planned before the 2028 season. MORE: KKR retention list for IPL 2027: Retained and released players Franchises haven’t waited for the deadline to start reshaping their squads. Mumbai Indians and Punjab Kings completed a swap built around Hardik Pandya and Arshdeep Singh on November 11; Chennai Super Kings and Sunrisers Hyderabad agreed a four-player exchange a few days earlier, and Delhi Capitals and Lucknow Super Giants had already pulled off the Rishabh Pant–Kuldeep Yadav deal in June. For fans trying to follow all this, the vocabulary can feel confusing, since the three options sound similar but work in completely different ways. The Cricket News explains how retention, release and trade differ, what each does to a team’s salary cap and what recent deals reveal about the rules in practice. MORE: IPL 2027 auction: Three teams that can sign Aaryavir Sehwag at the mini-auction after U-19 Asia Cup heroics PL 2027 mini-auction rules: Salary cap, squad size and key dates The headline number this season is the salary cap. The total cap was ₹110 crore in 2024, then rose to ₹146 crore in 2025 and ₹151 crore in 2026, and it stands at ₹157 crore for 2027. It’s worth being careful here, because this figure is not the same thing as the auction purse. The total salary cap is made up of the auction purse, incremental performance pay and match fees, with match fees set at ₹7.5 lakh for each playing member, the Impact Player included. The auction purse alone has been reported at ₹130 crore for this season, which is a ₹5 crore increase from 2026. item.title: Germany remains third in Group B behind Netherlands and Greece despite Nations League victory over Serbia
item.description: Photo by Pedja Milosavljevic / AFP via Getty Images | AFP via Getty Images An own goal by Srđan Babić, followed by goals from Florian Wirtz and Brajan Gruda, ensured three points for Jürgen Klopp’s men against a nine-man Serbia. Despite conceding a goal in the 56th minute, Germany ultimately made light work of the Balkans as the game ended 3-1. However, the three points only put Germany third place in Group B at the end of Matchday Five, leaving Die Mannschaft in a precarious position. Group table ahead of Monday's final matchday Germany vs Netherlands in Berlin pic.twitter.com/4Sxyh6D3I2 — Bayern & Germany (@iMiaSanMia) November 13, 2026 Germany drew level with Greece on eight points after the Netherlands 7-0 demolition over Ivan Jovanović’s side. However, Germany still trail the Greeks despite boasting superior goal difference. In the Nations League, UEFA prioritises head-to-head results over goal difference. Therefore, Greece still hold an advantage over Germany going into Matchday Six. Jovanović’s side also has the easier fixture against Serbia, leaving Germany the tricky task of conquering an in-form Netherlands side to book their ticket to the quarterfinals. Jurgen Klopp’s men could still sneak into the knockouts with a draw against the Oranje, provided Serbia beats Greece. But given the Serbia’s poor form, three points are practically guaranteed for the Greeks, making Germany’s mission against the Netherlands straightforward: win. Join the conversation! item.title: Mohya reveals "cool guy" Klopp led him to pick Germany over Morocco
item.description: Mohya reveals "cool guy" Klopp led him to pick Germany over Morocco Wael Mohya has revealed that DFB head coach Jürgen Klopp was the reason behind his decision to represent Germany over Morocco. “Morocco have made no secret of their interest in having me represent them," Mohya was quoted as saying by Sport BILD. "However, my parents are from there, so the country is part of my family, and I have huge respect for it. "But the way Jürgen Klopp spoke to me meant I didn't have to think twice about whether to accept this call-up. "He [Klopp] convinced me with what he had to say, and then I immediately realised what a really cool guy he is. “I'm looking forward to spending the coming period with him on the pitch, and I'm convinced that he will help me improve as well,” he added. Mohya was left out of the DFB squad which beat Serbia 3-1 but could potentially make his debut against the Netherlands on Monday.

item.title: “Corrupted Zebras,” “Refs Have Been Atrocious”: Texas Fans Fume at Referees for Missing Horse Collar Penalty As Arch Manning Throws INT vs. LSU
item.description: Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning - SEC Football Kickoff Media Day © IMAGN Arch Manning finished the first half of Saturday’s game against LSU with just nine completions for 82 yards and an interception. However, fans believe his turnover should never have happened. Replay footage showed Tigers defensive lineman Jordan Ross performing what appeared to be a horse-collar tackle on the Texas quarterback during that play: When the referees did not call a penalty, fans were outraged: “Corrupted zebras,” one sneered. “The refs in this game have been atrocious,” one rued. “How do you miss this?” another shuddered. “Unbelievable,” one sighed. “One of the worst missed calls I’ve ever seen,” another proclaimed. “NOW: BLATANT ROBBERY AGAINST TEXAS,” another “reported”. Manning also carried the ball five times for 32 yards and a score. Meanwhile, LSU QB Sam Leavitt threw for 173 yards and two touchdowns – both to Jackson Harris – and as many interceptions. Arch Manning outranked by Big 12 WR in draft expert’s Top 50 prospects list If Arch Manning enters next year’s NFL draft, he stands to be the headliner of an intriguing cast of prospects that is also expected to include Oregon’s Dante Moore. However, at least one person thinks someone else from a usually unheralded program is a better player than him. In his recent Top 50 prospect rankings, The Athletic’s Dane Brugler put Reed Harris over the Texas quarterback (24th vs. 25th). The Arizona State wideout entered Week 12 as one of the Big 12’s top receivers, leading the conference with 907 yards. Brugler wrote (via Arizona Sports): “A high school quarterback, Harris is a big athlete who looks more natural than expected framing the football. He has the speed to stack corners, but also the physicality to win crowded targets and keep his balance after the catch to find the hidden yardage.” The 2027 NFL draft will be held on the National Mall in Washington, DC, from April 29 to May 1. item.title: The 10 longest unbeaten runs in men's international football history
item.description: The 10 longest unbeaten runs in men's international football history Going unbeaten in international football is a remarkable achievement, but sustaining that success over several years is an entirely different challenge. A select group of national teams have managed to put together extraordinary runs without defeat, establishing themselves among the most dominant sides in international football history. Spain currently hold the record. The world and European champions extended their unbeaten run to 43 matches with a 2-0 win in Czechia in the Nations League last week. La Roja have not lost since a friendly defeat to Colombia in March 2024, enjoying European Championship and World Cup success during that period. We look at the 10 longest unbeaten runs in men's international football history. Longest unbeaten runs in men's international football history Spain have surged past the previous record of 37 matches, set by Italy between 2018 and 2021. Despite a difficult recent period that has included consecutive World Cup misses, the Azzurri went 37 games without defeat across that period, winning Euro 2020 under Roberto Mancini. Remarkably, six of the 10 longest unbeaten international runs have been recorded in the last decade. Spain (3), Argentina (2) and Morocco (2) all feature multiple times inside the top 10.

item.title: Notre Dame has already started its college football playoff run
item.description: Nov 14, 2026; South Bend, Indiana, USA; Notre Dame Fighting Irish cornerback Christian Gray (29) celebrates a stop against the Boston College Eagles during the second half at Notre Dame Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Michael Caterina-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Notre Dame Fighting Irish probably play more playoff football than anyone in the country. That statement isn’t a brag, it’s just the reality Notre Dame has been living for the last three seasons — and it’s mostly their own fault. In 2024, Notre Dame lost to Northern Illinois in the second game of the season, and they played win or go home football all the way to the National Championship game against Ohio State. In 2025, Notre Dame lost two very close games to start the season, and then went on to pound the rest of their 10 opponents until the playoff committees executed the PROTECT ALABAMA GAMEPLAN, and left the Irish stranded in South Bend. 2026 is very much the same as both 2024 and 2025. After the loss to BYU, there was no room for error for the Irish — especially when they were initially ranked No. 11 in the first CFP rankings as opposed to their No. 4 AP Top 25 ranking. The Miami game (because who really cares about the Navy game) was the first playoff game of 2026 for the Irish. They don’t get the special treatment that everyone believes they do — that alone is for the circle jerking of the SEC (obviously). After Notre Dame’s win over Miami, a few of the talking heads in the media tried selling people the idea that even if the Irish do drop one of their last three games — they’re still probably IN the playoffs. The unproven truth, however, is that those statements are FALSE and misleading as hell. The bigger discourse going on right now isn’t about which teams are getting into the CFP, it’s about which conferences get what number in the playoff. All Notre Dame has to do is slip, and this committee will be ready to push them off of a cliff. All of THAT is why Notre Dame’s 41-7 win over Boston College is fairly encouraging. The Irish were coming off of a huge win, and on a gloomy and cold day, they went out there and beat the hell out of a crappy team. I know that doesn’t sound exciting, but it shows how locked in this Notre Dame team is right now. The Irish went out there and put up 500 yards of offense, and gave up just 136 yards. Jonaz Walton, alone, outgained the entire Boston College team. Notre Dame has two games left of the regular season — which is basically just a couple of “play in” games. None of it has to be pretty, as an 11-1 Irish team who is currently ranked No. 5 in the CFP rankings is a lock to get in the thing. Still, as it is with any playoff run, Notre Dame has to be absolutely locked in to the task at hand. In doing that, Notre Dame should win these games by a good margin — and then it’s onto round two of the playoffs (which is actually round one or a bye week).

item.title: Rudi Garcia opens up on losing Man United job to Ralf Rangnick in 2021
item.description: Rudi Garcia opens up on losing Man United job to Ralf Rangnick in 2021 Former Belgium manager Rudi Garcia has opened up on applying for the Manchester United job. The Red Devils have just completed another managerial upheaval at Old Trafford, with Mauricio Pochettino appointed as Michael Carrick’s replacement. The Englishman was dismissed earlier this week after a disappointing run that has seen the English giants manage just three wins in 15 games across all competitions this season. United have registered just one win in 10 Premier League games, and are 18th in the league table at the moment. Meanwhile, Pochettino, who is currently in charge of the United States men’s national team, will depart his position next week after the game against Haiti and take charge at the Theatre of Dreams. Fans will hope that the Argentine can finally break the vicious managerial cycle that has gripped the Red Devils since Sir Alex Ferguson left the club. Pochettino becomes eighth permanent United manager in just over a decade Pochettino will take charge as United’s eighth permanent manager in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. The legendary Scot retired in the summer of 2013 and the Red Devils are still struggling to replicate his success story at the Theatre of Dreams. The English giants initially appointed David Moyes as Sir Alex’s successor, but he was removed from his position before the end of the season. Louis van Gaal came in next, won the FA Cup and departed in the summer of 2016. José Mourinho took over as the Dutchman’s replacement, and secured the Europa League and the EFL Cup before things went haywire in his third season. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer was initially appointed as the Portuguese’s temporary replacement, before securing the full-time job after a wonderful run. The Norwegian’s spell showed tremendous promise, but United failed to back him in the transfer market and the vicious cycle struck again. Solskjaer lost his job in November 2021 and the Red Devils initially considered Garcia as his replacement. The Frenchman has now opened up on his talks with the club management. Page 1 of 2 1 2 United interviewed Garcia for managerial position Speaking to The Athletic , Garcia revealed that he interviewed for the hot seat at Old Trafford after Ole Gunnar Solskjaer departed in December 2021. He said: “Yes, I interviewed twice to work in this fantastic club, one of the best clubs in the world.” “I’d like to work in England and I met Darren Fletcher and John Murtough. It was an interim role and they asked me what I would do once it was over. I told them I would do so well that I would be staying in Manchester, but they gave the job to Ralf.” Ralf Rangnick was selected for the job and guided the team to a sixth-placed finish before Erik ten Hag took charge in the summer of 2022. The Dutchman was replaced by Ruben Amorim in November 2024, who then made way for Carrick in January this year, before the job fell to Pochettino this month. Garcia, meanwhile, took char

item.title: Ryan Leonard Could Face Supplemental Discipline
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - APRIL 12: Ryan Leonard #9 of the Washington Capitals skates against the Pittsburgh Penguins on April 12, 2026 at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C. (Photo by Jamie Sabau/Getty Images) Getty Washington Capitals right winger Ryan Leonard earned a double minor for high sticking against the New Jersey Devils Saturday. The second-year winger clipped New Jersey Devils center Cody Glass above the eye in a dangerous looking play that could draw the attention of NHL Player Safety. Ryan Leonard High Sticking Penalty Leonard, 21, had just played the puck on a breakout when Glass approached and Leonard swung his stick, catching the Glass over the eye. Ryan Leonard received a double minor for swinging his stick at Cody Glass’s head 😬 Suspension coming? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/2IiWmW1H5F — Gino Hard (@GinoHard_) November 15, 2026 The infraction earned Leonard a double-minor penalty. Glass did not miss significant time and finished the game with one assist in 11:20 of ice time. The Capitals lost Saturday’s game by a score of 7-4, dropping both games against the Devils this week. This is the kind of play, either through intent or merely careless play with the stick, that should draw a second look from NHL Player Safety. This is Ryan Leonard’s second season in the National Hockey League. Through 18 games, he has six goals and six assists for 12 points. Three of his six goals have come via the power play. Glass had been off to a slow start, but his assist on Saturday night extended his point streak to four games. He scored a career high 19 goals last season but has just two goals and six points through 21 games this season. Up Next for the Capitals After back-to-back losses to New Jersey, the Capitals will visit the Tampa Bay Lightning on Tuesday. Washington then returns home to face the Buffalo Sabres on Thursday before visiting Boston on Saturday. If Leonard gets suspended, the Capitals may need to fill his spot in the lineup for these upcoming games. Wingers Ethen Frank and Ivan Miroshnichenko were healthy scratches for the Capitals on Saturday. Either one could be called on if Leonard is going to miss any time. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Ryan Leonard Could Face Supplemental Discipline appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Should the Bruins Keep 30-Goal Pace Forward Or Sell High?
item.description: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 12: Casey Mittelstadt #11 of the Boston Bruins looks on during the first period against the Montréal Canadiens at TD Garden on November 12, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Getty Casey Mittelstadt has seven goals in 20 games. That puts him on roughly a 30-goal pace over 84 games. When GM Don Sweeney traded Charlie Coyle for Will Zellers, a second-round pick, and a top-six winger who has suddenly become second in goals behind the Bruins’ David Pastrnak, it looked like a pretty good deal. But beneath the surface, this hot start might lead the Bruins to make a key decision. Should the Bruins Sell High? Middelstadt had a solid run with the Buffalo Sabres. As a member of the Bruins, his early 2026-27 run has become better than good. He noted, “Being in the same spot for a couple years now, I feel very comfortable here. I think it maybe takes me a little bit more time than normal people. So yeah, I think that’s been huge for me too.” Now that he’s gotten more comfortable, should the Bruins double down and hope he’s a key part of their future or move on while he looks appealing to the rest of the league? Mittelstadt is scoring at a 25 percent clip. He has seven goals on 28 shots. But his shooting average is only around 13 percent, and over an 84-game stretch, this elite percentage is likely to regress. He has good skill, and he’s fitting in. But he might not be the kind of player the Bruins should sign to a big contract, even though he’s off to a very hot start this season. The reality is that both Mittelstadt and Pavel Zacha, who makes $4.75 million, are in contract seasons. Mittelstadt makes $5.75 million, and both will become UFAs. What do they do? If Mittelstadt finishes near 30 goals, he won’t settle for a small raise. He’ll ask for $7 million or more on the market. The core question now is whether they should pay free-agent prices for a 28-year-old winger whose numbers might be inflated this season because of his high shooting percentage. The Bruins Have Players Ready for the Next Step The deal is that giving Middelstadt a bigger contract might slow the development of some of Boston’s younger players. James Hagens is out for a few weeks on IR with a back injury, but he’s already shown he can be a top-six player, perhaps on the second line. There are also a number of other players in the next wave, including Matt Poitras, Dean Letourneau, who’s playing with Boston College and doing really well, and Will Zellers, the prospect the Bruins got in the trade involving Coyle. Perhaps there are two good choices here. If Mittelstadt proves to be solid all season long and has a career season, keep him. But you don’t want to put him in the way of other youngsters who are coming up through the ranks. He could be a trade bargain . Or he could just be the kind of player you keep around and see what he does. If Boston has a legitimate playoff team, why would you move somebody who’s so productive?

item.title: The needless trend illustrated by Spain v England that is hurting football
item.description: Had football kept one simple little fascination, it would be hard not to indulge Declan Rice’s typical enthusiasm . “You are going away to the Metropolitano, playing the world champions in a game to see who can top the group,” the midfielder said of England ’s game in Madrid on Sunday. “We have a massive motive… to beat Spain as the away team would be a massive thing for us.” In other words, the benchmark. This is the level England will have to reach to win Euro 2028 , as both Rice and Thomas Tuchel expounded on. Except, for all the grandeur that the midfielder described, Uefa have lessened the stakes. In the first two iterations of the Nations League , this game at the Metropolitano would not just be a game to win the group but a direct qualification play-off. Only the first-placed teams went through. The rematch of Spain v England promises to be interesting but has less jeopardy than it should (Getty) And sure, it might not be the World Cup or the Euros, but the very prospect of elimination from a competition that does at least mean something would have naturally made this fixture more compelling. As it is, with both teams secure in the top two well ahead of Croatia and Czech Republic, there’s a question over whether they will even play their best sides. None of this is to say the game won’t be as enjoyable as the brilliant September meeting , it’s just that it’s not what it could have been. And that fits with a needless trend in football right now. The current game apparently has an obsession with safety nets – something to catch the endless bloat. Everything that could have expanded has expanded. The expansion of the Nations League has taken the edge off today’s game (Getty Images) Uefa themselves started this with the Euros. In 2016, a total of 16 teams became 24, with 16 also going through to the knockout stages. The clean binary symmetry of the old two-from-four groups was gone. A team’s chances of a fourth game were expanded from 50 per cent to 67 per cent, bringing with them the convolutions of the best third-placed sides going through. More safety nets. In 2019, the Uefa model was followed by both the Asian Football Confederation and Confederation of African Football, who made the same changes to their continental competitions. In 2024, it was Uefa’s own club competitions, creating the “football wallpaper” of the Champions League opening stage. The Champions League group phase has become ‘football wallpaper’ (Getty) That has obviously had a lot of discussion, including on these very pages, and Uefa do have different reasons for the expansion of the Nations League. They’re well aware that the old tournament qualification systems of two-year build-ups no longer work, especially because the Euros has expanded. Games were certainly meaning less there. They could see it in the broadcasting figures, and knew they needed to do something. The Nations League is a smart solution, especially as it serves to constrict qualification to actually make

item.title: Real Madrid star continues his recovery in Brazil as he nears return to full fitness – report
item.description: Real Madrid star continues his recovery in Brazil as he nears return to full fitness – report The Real Madrid physical team has done an exceptional job when it comes to neutralising the amount of fresh injuries, all thanks to Jose Mourinho’s new-look setup. Players who are on the sidelines still are mostly nursing injuries from last season, such as Rodrygo, who is still yet to feature in a single game this season. Recent reports have indicated that the player is in the final phase of his recovery and could return to action before the end of the year. Rodrygo continues recovery in Brazil As reported by Mundo Deportivo , Rodrygo has continued his recovery back home in Brazil during the international break. Rodrygo hasn’t played football since his injury in March. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The forward, who suffered a serious injury in March, rupturing the ACL and the external meniscus in his right leg, had to go through surgery. Since then, the player has been working hard towards a return, ideally before the end of the year. In recent days, that work has taken place in his homeland, Brazil. Rodrygo was recently seen attending the Formula One Grand Prix in Sao Paulo, where he visited the paddock of some of the teams. He also paid a visit to the facilities of Santos, his former club, where he continued his recovery program. The entire process is being carefully overseen by Real Madrid. The club are aware that Rodrygo’s comeback is drawing closer, but they have no intention of rushing him back to action. When will Rodrygo return? Mourinho would welcome the return of Rodrygo. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Everything suggests Rodrygo could return to action sooner rather than later, most likely before the turn of the year. The Brazilian international is expected to be back under Mourinho’s disposal at some point in December, with the player particularly eyeing a return to action in the Copa Del Rey. It was reported earlier that Rodrygo wants to back for Real Madrid’s first Copa Del Rey tie of the campaign, scheduled for December 16. That fixture is likely to be played against a lower-division opposition, thus giving Rodrygo an ideal opportunity to return to the pitch in a relatively low-pressure setting.

item.title: ‘I felt my leg…’ – Dominik Szoboszlai makes worrying injury admission after Hungary win
item.description: ‘I felt my leg…’ – Dominik Szoboszlai makes worrying injury admission after Hungary win Dominik Szoboszlai has given an update on his knee injury after Hungary’s win over Georgia on Saturday, and his comments could be quite concerning for Liverpool fans. The midfielder’s involvement for his country during this international window was placed in doubt after the knock that he incurred in the Reds’ victory at Crystal Palace last weekend, although he still linked up with Marco Rossi’s squad for their UEFA Nations League fixtures. The Hungarian FA had deferred any decision on whether the 26-year-old would play until the last minute , but he featured for the entirety of his nation’s 2-0 triumph in Tbilisi and claimed the assist for Barnabas Varga’s clinching goal. Szoboszlai almost pulled out of Hungary win Szoboszlai revealed after the match that he nearly pulled out of playing after he felt a twinge during the warm-up prior to kick-off, but his determination to feature would eventually prevail. In quotes relayed by Nemzeti Sport , the Hungary captain said: “I was always 100% sure that I would be able to play, but the doctors were less sure. I progressed day by day, focused on myself, received treatment. “I played with my leg for a training session and a half, and in the warm-up I was close to cancelling it because I felt my leg on one of the shots, but if I’ve come this far, I won’t let the team down. Now the treatment starts all over again. I have to be ready again by Tuesday.” (Photo by Charles McQuillan/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Szoboszlai’s comments will worry Liverpool fans Szoboszlai’s comments may well come as a worry to Liverpool fans, with the midfielder admitting that he played through the pain barrier and seemingly defied the assessment of medical professionals. His remark about getting ready for Hungary’s match against Northern Ireland on Tuesday night will also have Andoni Iraola sweating, with the 26-year-old set to push himself for a tight turnaround even though he seems nowhere near full fitness. It’s natural that, as captain of his country, the Reds’ number 8 will stop at nothing to try and be available for them, but his club will be left praying that he comes through the Magyars’ next game unscathed. Szoboszlai will return from international duty into a hectic run of 11 Liverpool fixtures before the end of December, and we’ll need him and his teammates to be operating at their best throughout that busy period. For everyone at Anfield, Hungary’s match on Tuesday will be monitored with frayed nerves to see if the midfielder comes through without any further complications in his knee.
