LSU’s Lane Kiffin Reveals Honest Mindset After Blowing 2-Score Lead Against Texas
item.description: BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 14: Head Coach Lane Kiffin of the Louisiana State Tigers and Head Coach Steve Sarkisian of the Texas Longhorns interact on the field after the game at Tiger Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) Getty LEXINGTON, KENTUCKY - OCTOBER 10: Lane Kiffin the head coach of the LSU Tigers gives instructions to his team against the Kentucky Wildcats at Kroger Field on October 10, 2026 in Lexington, Kentucky. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) Getty The LSU football team is in the first season of the Lane Kiffin era. Unfortunately for Kiffin, his team is now 6-4 after letting a two-score lead slip away in a 22-21 loss to Texas on Saturday night. Building the program he wants may take time, but that does not make another missed opportunity any easier to accept. Getty LEXINGTON, KENTUCKY – OCTOBER 10: Lane Kiffin the head coach of the LSU Tigers gives instructions to his team against the Kentucky Wildcats at Kroger Field on October 10, 2026 in Lexington, Kentucky. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) Afterward, Kiffin explained his frustration with a game LSU had chances to finish. The Tigers held the advantage before Arch Manning helped Texas put together the winning drive. Kiffin credited the Longhorns while acknowledging the disappointment his own team was left carrying. “Credit Texas for driving down and winning at the end of the game,” Kiffin said. “It was a really hard-fought game where both teams played really hard.” Lane Kiffin Laments LSU’s Missed Opportunities Against Texas This was not a case of Kiffin describing an opponent LSU could not compete with. His frustration came from believing the Tigers had done enough in several areas to put themselves in position to win. The ending made everything that came before it harder to stomach. “It’s really disappointing to be up two scores in the game and not be able to close it out,” Kiffin said. “We had plenty of opportunities.” LSU fans do not need much help understanding that feeling. Watching a lead disappear at home creates a different kind of frustration than simply getting beaten by a better performance. There is the result itself, followed by every moment supporters can identify when the outcome might have changed. “In a lot of areas we outplayed them to win the game, but again, that’s not how it works,” Kiffin said. “It doesn’t work that way.” LSU’s Final Breakdown Leaves Kiffin Frustrated That qualification matters. Kiffin was not claiming LSU should receive credit for a victory it failed to secure. He acknowledged that favorable stretches and opportunities mean little when the other team makes the decisive play. “I’m disappointed for our players and our fans,” Kiffin said. His explanation of the finish pointed toward a coverage mistake. item.title: Why This Bulls Center Is a Top Trade Target for Warriors
item.description: The Golden State Warriors are off to a strong start this season with an 8-5 record, but they’ve lost two straight, and an injury to Steph Curry , who was playing at an All-NBA level, has already set them back. The Warriors have gotten strong contributions from rookie Yaxel Lendeborg , who is averaging 20.2 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 3.5 assists. His play has helped offset the loss of Kristaps Porzingis, who was dealing with health issues and announced that he would be stepping away from basketball for the time being. The team could be looking elsewhere to help out in the frontcourt, as they are reportedly interested in Jalen Smith of the Chicago Bulls. NBA Insider Jake Fischer said on “Deals and Dunks” on SiriusXM NBA Radio that the Warriors have contacted the Bulls about Smith and strongly indicated that the Warriors are interested in Smith. He said that Smith was someone “high on Golden State’s list.” Smith was drafted tenth overall in 2020 by the Phoenix Suns. He was signed by the Bulls in the 2024 offseason. He is averaging 13 points, 7.8 rebounds, and two assists this season while shooting 51% from the field and 34% from three. He is in the final year of his deal, making $9 million this season before becoming an unrestricted free agent in the offseason. Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images Can The Warriors Get A Deal Done And Should They? The Warriors are reportedly looking to trade Porzingis and his $20 million contract, but they would need to attach draft compensation since Porzingis is unlikely to play this year, if ever again. The Warriors likely have no problem attaching some second-round picks to get Smith, but would they be willing to move off a first for a player who may only be there for one season? They have their own first from now until 2032, and if they are confident in their playoff positioning and Smith’s value, a deal could get done. The Bulls are continuing to rebuild, and though Smith has been good for them this season, he’s not a long-term player for them as an upcoming unrestricted free agent who is behind Nic Claxton and Caleb Wilson on the frontcourt depth chart. Otherwise, Golden State would have to deal some combination of Will Richard, Gary Payton, and De’Anthony Melton to make the money work. Payton and Melton can’t be traded until December 15. If the Warriors can get a deal done for Smith, they should take the swing. Draymond Green is logging minutes at the center position right now, as Al Horford is 40 and can’t play the heavy minutes he used to, and Porzingis is absent. Draymond at the five used to be the Warriors’ way of decimating teams, but those days are long gone and Draymond at the five is now an undersized option without the infrastructure and offense to carry things.

item.title: Nwifuru is silently taking Ebonyi to greater heights, and touching every sector
item.description: By Anayo Okoli The trending is narrative given to the public in and outside Ebonyi State by opposition is that Governor Francis Nwifuru is not working. And this narrative has gained currency among the people. But a visit to the state indicates that indeed the contrary is the case. The Governor is indeed doing working and touching every sector of development. The reality on ground is that a lot of development is happening in the State. Across the 13 local government areas of thespian state, no community is left out, at least with a road project. According to records, on assumption of office, Governor Francis Nwifuru unfolded what he called “People’s Charter of Needs” as a priority guide to his development trajectory and his administration has followed this religiously. In fact some of the ongoing projects are landmark projects that would project the state to national and even international maps. For instance, two specialized universities being built by the government will change the education landscape of the State. One of them, the ICT University has taken off at a temporary site with over 100 students receiving education free of charge. Work at the permanent site in Oferekpe, located in a vast land space, is ongoing with many sections, including lecturers quarters, classroom blocks, Senate building, student hostels almost completed. Construction of a teaching hospital is also going at ICT University. There is also the Aeronautical University located not far from the Chuba Okadigbo airport. Government sources said that the National University Commission has accredited the University to take off next academic session. The university will train engineers of various specialties. Indeed, a lot of structures are springing up at the massive sites in an effort to be ready for the take off of academic activities. From what is on ground, Nwifuru is investing a lot in the education sector and manpower development. He has awarded full Masters and PhD scholarship sponsorship to 1,400 Ebonyi indigenous students to universities in the United Kingdom and Nigeria; renovated some structures at State University and raised its subvention from N150 million to N280 million as well as released N700 outstanding subvention to the institutions. He also extended the good gesture to the State College of Education, Ikwo, which he upgraded to a University of Education. Many dilapidated primary and secondary schools have been rehabilitated. About 2000 primary and secondary school teachers were recruited. These are some of the governor’s major undertakings in the education sector. In the health sector, the administration has also recorded a lot of progress. In its determination to change the narrative and make the residents of the State have access to quality healthcare, the government embarked on massive recruitment of healthcare workers. 653 medical personnel were employed across Ebonyi State, including doctors and other medical personnel. item.title: Meet 2 African countries to ever break into top five FIFA World Ranking
item.description: Only two African countries have ever reached the top five of the FIFA Men’s World Ranking, with Nigeria and Morocco achieving the historic feat more than three decades apart. The Super Eagles of Nigeria were the first African team to break into the world’s top five, reaching fifth place in April 1994. The achievement came during one of the most memorable periods in Nigerian football history, following the country’s victory at the 1994 Africa Cup of Nations in Tunisia. Nigeria, coached by Clemens Westerhof, had a talented generation featuring Rashidi Yekini, Daniel Amokachi, Emmanuel Amunike, Finidi George, Sunday Oliseh and Austin Jay-Jay Okocha. The Super Eagles also made their debut at the 1994 FIFA World Cup in the United States, where they topped their group before being eliminated by Italy in the round of 16. For 32 years, Nigeria’s fifth-place ranking remained the highest position ever achieved by an African national team. However, Morocco joined the exclusive list in September 2026 after climbing to fifth in the FIFA Men’s World Ranking. The Atlas Lions’ rise followed a period of impressive performances, including their historic run to the quarter-finals of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Morocco had also made history at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, becoming the first African country to reach the semi-finals of the competition. Their latest achievement saw them equal Nigeria’s record, making them the second African country to reach fifth place in the global ranking. According to FIFA, Morocco’s achievement matched the highest position ever attained by an African national team, a record Nigeria had held since April 1994. The two African countries are: Nigeria: Fifth place in April 1994. Morocco: Fifth place in September 2026. The two countries have therefore written their names into African football history, becoming the only representatives of the continent to reach the top five of the FIFA Men’s World Ranking. item.title: Mbappe available for clash with Turkey – Zidane
item.description: Kylian Mbappe is available to play in France’s final Nations League group fixture against Turkey, coach Zinedine Zidane said on Saturday, as Les Bleus seek a spot in the quarter-finals. Real Madrid forward Mbappe missed Thursday’s defeat to Group A1 leaders Italy with a hamstring problem, but Zidane confirmed: “He will be with us tomorrow (Sunday). Mbappe, who has netted 17 goals in all competitions for his club this season, was back in the France squad for this international break after missing his country’s previous three matches through injury. Zidane said Mbappe’s return “changes everything”, adding: “I’d rather have him with us than not.” The 54-year-old, a World Cup winner with France in 1998 and European champion two years later, denied any tensions with Mbappe and said his relationship with his star striker was going “perfectly”. “I can’t stop people saying what they’re saying, but it’s nonsense and quite irritating,” said Zidane. France are second in Group A1, level on 10 points with Italy, and need just a draw against Turkey in Bordeaux to secure qualification for the Nations League quarter-finals. item.title: Nigeria’s mission in S/Africa urges calm in row over Ramaphosa spokesman’s remarks
item.description: The Nigerian High Commission in South Africa has urged restraint and reconciliation after remarks by President Cyril Ramaphosa’s spokesman, Vincent Magwenya, about Nigeria’s High Commissioner, Mr Femi Fani-Kayode. The Mission said on its verified X handle that it wants cordial relations between both countries preserved. The row followed a disruption of the South African Presidency’s YouTube livestream when Fani-Kayode was due to present his letters of credence to Ramaphosa in Tshwane. The broadcast was restored while Ramaphosa was addressing the ambassadors. Magwenya had then accused Fani-Kayode of of lying about Ramaphosa intervening in the controversy surrounding his diplomatic credentials. The Mission said Fani-Kayode, one of the last diplomats to present credentials, complained that his speech had been deliberately omitted. It said he raised the matter with Ramaphosa, who apologised and assured him all was well. It said the disagreement should have been handled through diplomatic channels and urged Magwenya to show restraint. The Mission described Magwenya’s conduct as provocative and diplomatically inappropriate. It said its post was meant to reject what it called his attempt to portray Fani-Kayode as dishonest and to damage Nigeria’s image. “To us this matter is closed, but if you wish to escalate it you are welcome to do so and we are up to the task. A word is enough for the wise,” the Mission said. It commended Ramaphosa for intervening. “Thankfully your President had the decency and presence of mind to put out the fire and direct you and your state broadcaster to do the right thing. He literally saved the day,” it said. The post Nigeria’s mission in S/Africa urges calm in row over Ramaphosa spokesman’s remarks appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: My subjects are very loyal — HRM Albert Akpomudje (SAN), the Ohworode of Olomu Kingdom
item.description: By Akpokona Omafuaire The Ohworode of Olomu, HRM Albert Akpomudje, SAN, FCIArb, Eyavwien-Alaka I, is marking his first year coronation anniversary. In this interview, Akpomuje bares his mind on his experience as a traditional ruler, Chairman, Body of Benchers and a practising lawyer. Excerpts: Your Majesty, it’s been one year since you ascended the throne. What has been your experience as the traditional ruler of ancient Olomu Kingdom? Well, I must say it’s been a very exciting one year. First of all, I must commend my subjects on the fact that since after the coronation on the 15th of November, 2025, they have been very, very loyal. After the coronation I decided to go round the 15 communities under Olomu Kingdom, and the excitement of the people during the time gave me a very positive and commendable impression of the people; it was like they were seeing their king for the first time visiting their communities, which had not happened before. They did everything to make the occasion memorable. That encouraged me to say I have loyal subjects in Olomu Kingdom. How have you been coping with your legal practice and also continuing your role as the Chairman of Body of Benchers? Well, it’s not been easy. But I want to thank God who has given me the strength and good health to be able to manage three things or four together. One, I still go to my office to do what I’m used to. What I don’t do frequently now is maybe going to court, but I’m on ground. I’m still in charge of the office, and I have very able juniors. Then, of course, the Body of Benchers, I have to be on ground in Abuja for meetings and so many other things and then you have to come back to the traditional set up. But I want to thank God that I’ve been coping well. It is exciting. I know that it is not too easy. It’s not something you can say it’s exhausting, but, at the same time, I’m enjoying it because these are three different things which I have to cope with. But I’ve enjoyed every bit of it. I’ve coped very well with the Body of Benchers to the extent that I have been dining with students in almost all the campuses. I go to the campus to dine with them, the statutory dining terms, and at the home front I am on ground, so I’m not lacking in anything. One year down the lane, do you regret your decision to accept being the Ohworode of Olomu Kingdom? I can never regret it. I think it is God’s divine arrangements you know, it is God’s favour on me; even though it’s not something I thought of before in my life. And the reason why I’m enjoying it is that I’m having cooperation from my people. So far, there are no issues. I don’t have issues with them. They rely on me. They respect me, and they do everything to show to me that they are ready to do anything as far as the kingdom is concerned, once it comes from me. item.title: CHINA DIARIES: The Future of farming
item.description: When we talk about China’s development, the images that often come to mind are high-speed trains, towering skyscrapers, electric vehicles and impressive infrastructure. But there is another quiet revolution taking place, one that is just as important to China’s future: agriculture. I had an opportunity to explore this during a visit to Yangling, in Shaanxi Province, a place that has become an important centre for agricultural science, research, innovation and technology. Our visit took us to three facilities: the SCO Demonstration Base for Agricultural Technology Exchange and Training, the Yangling Smart Agriculture Demonstration Park, and Yangling Liangke Agricultural Science and Technology Co. Ltd. What I saw offered an interesting glimpse into how China is using science and technology to rethink farming, improve productivity and strengthen food security. China Diaries: An Emperor, 8,000 Soldiers and a Lesson for Nigeria! 2027: We’ll fight Tinubu in South, North-Central, sweep North-West, North-East – Amaechi And, naturally, it got me thinking about Nigeria. Where farming meets the digital age One of the most interesting parts of the visit was seeing how technology is being integrated into everyday agricultural activities. At the smart agriculture demonstration facility, I saw a control station where plants are monitored through screens. Rather than relying entirely on physical observation, information about growing conditions can be monitored centrally, allowing operators to keep track of what is happening inside the growing facilities. It was a reminder that modern farming is increasingly becoming a data-driven activity. The farmer of the future may still walk through the farm, inspect the crops and get his hands dirty, but technology is giving him additional tools to make better decisions. I also saw vegetables being cultivated indoors in a controlled environment. It was fascinating to see food production taking place in a setting that looked quite different from the conventional farms we are familiar with in Nigeria. The idea is to manage growing conditions and create a more controlled environment for production. Such systems can help reduce dependence on some external weather conditions and make production more predictable, although their commercial viability depends on energy, infrastructure and operating costs. Another interesting sight was the display of grains and seedlings. These may look ordinary at first glance, but they represent an important part of the agricultural value chain: research, seed development and the effort to improve the quality and productivity of crops before they even get to the farm. Then came the agricultural drones. I photographed drones designed to spray farmland. Their use illustrates how technology can help farmers cover large areas more efficiently and apply agricultural treatments with greater precision. item.title: Igando accident: Woman killed as Lexus rams into commercial bus
item.description: …LASEMA responds to three emergencies across Lagos, rescues stranded motorists By Matthew Johnson A woman has been killed after a Lexus car rammed into a commercial minibus at Igando, Lagos State, in an accident that also left the bus driver injured. The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) disclosed this while reporting its response to three separate emergencies across the state. The fatal accident occurred in the early hours of Friday, November 13, 2026, around Ajay Hotel, Igando, involving a Lexus car, a commercial minibus popularly known as Korope, and a pedestrian. According to preliminary information released by LASEMA, the Lexus car, which was reportedly fleeing, rammed into the minibus with registration number SMK 514 YG, causing the vehicle to strike the woman. The woman died in the incident, while the minibus driver sustained injuries and was taken to hospital before the arrival of the agency’s response team. Her remains were subsequently handed over to her relatives by officers of the Nigeria Police Force, Igando Division, in accordance with established procedures. LASEMA said its Dolphin Team, stationed in Igando, was immediately deployed after receiving a distress call and arrived at the scene within minutes. The agency, working alongside the Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA), Lagos Neighbourhood Safety Corps and the police, secured the accident scene, managed traffic and coordinated the removal of the affected vehicle. The minibus was recovered and towed to the Igando Police Station with the assistance of a private tow truck, while normal traffic flow was restored. In a statement signed by LASEMA’s Permanent Secretary, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, the state government expressed condolences to the family of the deceased and wished the injured driver a speedy recovery. Oke-Osanyintolu also disclosed that the agency attended to two other emergencies within the same operational period. At Ketu-Epe Road, LASEMA concluded its follow-up response to an earlier accident involving a white minibus that plunged into a ditch. Police officers at the scene confirmed that the driver and three passengers were receiving treatment at Ketu General Hospital. The permanent secretary said the vehicle was not obstructing traffic and that the incident had been formally handed over to the police at Ketu Division for further action. In another operation, LASEMA’s Lion Squad responded to a broken-down trailer conveying a 40-foot container along Imota Road, inward Ikorodu, around Agbowa. The trailer had developed a mechanical fault, obstructing a substantial portion of the road and posing a potential danger to other motorists. item.title: Kano drug war: PCN denies shielding illicit drug dealers
item.description: …says 1,631 drug outlets sealed in 2026, challenges task force chairman to provide evidence of alleged staff involvement By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) has denied allegations that it is shielding illicit drug dealers and facilitating the distribution of controlled substances in Kano State, insisting that it remains committed to enforcing pharmaceutical regulations. The council described the allegations by the Chairman of the Kano State Multi-Agency Taskforce on Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking, Muhuyi Magaji Rimin-Gado, as baseless and misleading, challenging him to provide verifiable evidence to substantiate his claims. In a rebuttal issued on Saturday and signed by Pharm. Hasiya Ladan, Consultant Pharmacist at the PCN Kano State Office, on behalf of the Registrar and Chief Executive Officer, the council disclosed that it sealed 1,631 pharmaceutical premises in Kano State in 2026 following inspections of 2,304 drug outlets. It also said 15 investigations into suspected regulatory violations were ongoing in the state, while its national enforcement team had visited Kano twice this year, in April and September. The rebuttal followed allegations made by Rimin-Gado at a press conference in Kano on November 14, where he accused the PCN and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) of allegedly protecting drug dealers operating in the state. The task force chairman had, among other things, questioned the circumstances surrounding the issuance of import licences to pharmaceutical companies dealing in pregabalin, particularly after NAFDAC rescheduled the drug as a controlled substance on September 14, 2026. He also accused the PCN of registering a pharmaceutical outlet at No. 10 Apple Avenue, allegedly located in a residential area, which he claimed was being used as a concealed distribution point for the drug. Rimin-Gado further alleged that some PCN officials were involved in clandestine drug businesses and questioned the council’s capacity to effectively regulate pharmaceutical activities in Kano, citing its relatively small number of personnel in the state. However, the PCN maintained that the regulation of pharmaceutical premises was a statutory federal responsibility backed by the Constitution, legislation and judicial pronouncements. It cited Item 21 of Part I of the Second Schedule to the 1999 Constitution, arguing that drugs and poisons fall under the Exclusive Legislative List and that their regulation is therefore the responsibility of the Federal Government through authorised agencies. The council also referenced the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (Establishment) Act 2022, the Supreme Court judgment in Pharmacists Board of Nigeria v. Franklin Adegbesote (1986), and a February 16, 2024 judgment of the Federal High Court, Kano, as legal authorities affirming its regulatory mandate. item.title: When grandpas, grandmas become cocaine smugglers
item.description: …404 ‘arrested’ in 20 months By Nnamdi Ojiego The image of an elderly grandmother or grandfather being led away by anti-narcotics officers over alleged involvement in drug trafficking is one that challenges conventional perceptions of who participates in the illicit drug trade. Yet, a succession of arrests involving people in their 60s, 70s and even older has brought an uncomfortable question to the fore: Why are people who should ordinarily be enjoying their retirement years becoming involved in the dangerous business of transporting, storing and distributing illicit drugs? In Nigeria, the figures supplied by Femi Babafemi, spokesperson of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) suggest that the phenomenon deserves closer attention. The agency arrested 240 persons aged 60 and above for drug-related offences in 2025, comprising 191 men and 49 women. Between January and August 2026, another 164 elderly suspects, including 128 men and 36 women, were arrested. The figures bring the total number of elderly persons arrested within the 20-month period to 404. Men accounted for the overwhelming majority, representing approximately 80 per cent of the arrests in 2025 and 78 per cent in the first eight months of 2026. Calculated strategy Although the 2026 figures cover only eight months and cannot be directly compared with the full-year 2025 total, the number of arrests already recorded points to the continued involvement of older people in drug-related activities. It also raises questions about the circumstances drawing them into a trade whose consequences include lengthy imprisonment, financial ruin, damaged family relationships and, in some cases, serious health risks. The NDLEA also reported seizing 6,998.77 kilogrammes of illicit drugs in connection with elderly suspects in 2025, compared with 1,479.988 kilogrammes between January and August 2026. From couriers to local dealers The cases recorded by the NDLEA in 2026 provide a glimpse into the different ways older people are becoming involved in the illicit drug trade. On March 14, 2026, NDLEA operatives arrested 74-year-old Ikwuakalom Nwakoro Emeka at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, while he was preparing to board a British Airways flight to London. The agency alleged that 11 kilogrammes of cocaine were discovered in his luggage, concealed in food items, including ground dry pepper. He reportedly told investigators he was travelling to Britain on holiday. Barely three months later, another high-profile case emerged at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos. On June 28, operatives arrested 67-year-old Mary Yetunde Barek, a Nigerian-British woman who worked as a caregiver in the United Kingdom, while she was preparing to board a Virgin Atlantic flight to London. The NDLEA alleged that 13 kilogrammes of cocaine were recovered from 31 large packages concealed in plantain peels designed to resemble actual plantain hands and packed among other food items. item.title: 60 DAYS TO POLLS: Fear over electoral process as political attacks rise
item.description: …Report says 640 killed in October as a result of broader insecurity …Experts warn against violence, fake news By Nnamdi Ojiego 60 days to the 2027 general elections, concerns are mounting over the safety of the electoral process as rising insecurity, attacks on political gatherings and the spread of misinformation threaten to undermine citizens’ participation in the polls. The concerns have been heightened by fresh incidents of political violence in different parts of the country, including Calabar, Cross River State, Asaba, Delta State, and Sokoto, where political supporters and opposition figures have reportedly come under attack. The developments have renewed questions about the preparedness of security agencies to protect candidates, party supporters and voters, particularly in a country already grappling with banditry, insurgency, kidnapping and communal violence. A report by the Centre for Democracy and Development (CDD), Nigeria Election Security Tracker for October 2026 provides a troubling picture of the security situation. It recorded 640 deaths during the month (October), representing a 61.62 per cent increase from the 396 deaths recorded in September. Of the 640 deaths, 638 were attributed to broader insecurity, while two resulted from election-related attacks in Enugu and Ebonyi. The North-East accounted for the highest number of fatalities, with 409 deaths. The report also documented 16 election-related incidents in October, compared with 14 in September, representing a 14.29 per cent increase. Attacks on campaign gatherings and convoys accounted for 11 of the 16 incidents. Other cases involved assaults on individuals, attacks on political property and the restriction of a political gathering. The incidents affected several political parties, including the All Progressives Congress (APC) and African Democratic Congress (ADC), which each recorded four cases, while the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) recorded three. Two of the incidents were fatal. Ifeanyi Nwolie died from gunshot injuries sustained during the NDC campaign launch in Enugu on October 10. In Ebonyi, gunmen attacked the convoy of NDC candidate, Rollins Offia-Nwali, on October 22, killing one person, injuring three others and burning his vehicle. The candidate reportedly escaped. The CDD report also documented attacks on ADC convoys in Igueben and Kogi, disruption of PDP consultations in Calabar, an attack on an ADC candidate’s meeting in Obosi, Anambra State, and the prevention of supporters from gathering for the Obi-Kwankwaso march in Abuja. Although broader insecurity accounted for most of the fatalities, the report warned that its consequences could extend to the electoral process, particularly in communities where residents have been displaced or roads have become unsafe. item.title: SpaceX returned its Starship rocket on Saturday—but there's a catch
item.description: STARBASE, Texas —The black and silver ship fell out of the sky, emerging from the cloud deck near the very end of its flight. Incongruously, the rocket flew horizontal until the last moment when three Raptor rocket engines ignited and it swooped into a vertical position. Slowly, gently, haltingly, the Starship upper stage eased its way toward the waiting tower where two arms extended outward, awaiting expectantly. The margins are so incredibly narrow. Two nubs on either side of the rocket, each protruding only about one foot, were the only purchase the rocket would have on the arms. Then, less than a minute after it came into view, the Starship upper stage was snagged by the launch tower, as snug as you like. And so it was all over. SpaceX, nearly a quarter of a century after its founding, had just taken a hugely significant step toward developing and optimizing a massive, rapidly reusable rocket. Read full article Comments

item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, has promised to resume oil exploration activities at the Kolmani oil field, which he said were suspended under the present administration. He also pledged to restore electricity subsidies and revive work on the abandoned Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project in the North-East. ﻿ Atiku made these promises during his presidential campaign rally in Bauchi State on Saturday. Speaking at the rally, he said, “I will restore electricity subsidies. I also promise to restore security in the North-East sub-region and the country at large. In the last general election, Atiku secured a significant number of votes in Bauchi State while contesting on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). item.title: 2027: I’m For Any Coalition That Supports Tinubu’s Re-Election — Gov Eno
item.description: Governor Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom State has thrown his weight behind the Rainbow Coalition led by Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike, saying that he will back any coalition that supports President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in the 2027 general elections. ﻿ Eno stated this while fielding questions during a media chat on Saturday. “That Rainbow Coalition is simply saying that we support President Tinubu as the President,” he said. “If I will join and be a member of any coalition — whether it is rainbow, call it any name. Any coalition that the central point is supporting the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, I am for it.” The governor said that the relationship between the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Akwa Ibom is “good on the ground”. Eno, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the APC after his defection from the PDP in June 2025, said the two parties had agreed to support Tinubu, the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, and himself in the 2027 general elections. “I will work with all of them, and I think we are good on the ground in Akwa Ibom when it comes to PDP-APC relationship,” the governor said. “We have agreed on the fact that we are supporting the President, we are supporting the Senate President, we are supporting the governor, and we have our clear understanding about those things.” The Rainbow Coalition is spearheaded by Wike to galvanise support for the re-election bid of President Tinubu in 2027. But the coalition has faced opposition from leaders of the APC. In October, 2026, Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma said that the Rainbow Coalition has no presence in the state. Speaking during the distribution of campaign vehicles under the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in the state, Uzodimma insisted that the APC would secure victory in the 2027 elections through organic votes. The governor maintained that the APC was the only recognised political party in the state and urged supporters to vote for the party’s candidates across all levels in the 2027 general elections. ﻿ Similarly, Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal told the minister to make his political position clear over his involvement with the coalition, insisting that he cannot simultaneously support the APC and other political parties. “Our message is very, very clear: be on one side, you can’t be on two sides. If you are in APC, please come out and support the APC, not you are supporting APC here, and you are supporting some other political parties somewhere else,” he said during an interview with Channels Television’s Inside Sources on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York in October. The post 2027: I’m For Any Coalition That Supports Tinubu’s Re-Election — Gov Eno appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 236 — Alienspotting
item.description: null On Episode 236 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. When we think of extraterrestrials, our minds generally go from the latex-suited bipedal aliens seen in Star Trek and Star Wars to more exotic critters in sci-fi movies. Scientists think in terms of carbon-based microbial life and other lower life forms. But some researchers, such as Tikhonov from Washington University, suggest that life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. He further suggests a new definition of life: something that takes in and transforms energy and replicates. His ideas radically expand our notions of alien life and how it might be recognized. Download or subscribe to this show at: https://twit.tv/shows/this-week-in-space . Get episodes ad-free with Club TWiT at https://twit.tv/clubtwit Space news of the week Watch SpaceX attempt a historic Starship launch and double-catch landing today Double-catch drama: Why Starship's Flight 15 is so important to SpaceX SpaceX's Starship megarocket will launch to orbit on Nov. 13. Will you be able to spot it in the night sky? item.title: Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show. Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. U.S. stock and bond markets are closed Saturday, but those levels still frame the weekend session. Nvidia is due to report third-quarter results on Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress, the first earnings release since Huang stepped down. item.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
item.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. Game over, man (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) There are still some scares hiding in here, though, ready to make complacent players jump out of their seats. Special Xenomorphs

item.title: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can’t trust AI CEOs
item.description: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy community, though she is perhaps best known for having served on the board of OpenAI, when she was one of four board members who voted to fire Sam Altman . That incident, now sometimes referred to as “the blip,” ended with Sam coming back as CEO, Helen resigning, and a new board of directors. OpenAI has since restructured entirely . But it’s worth remembering what Helen and the board were supposed to do: OpenAI’s nonprofit board existed specifically to make sure the company didn’t betray its mission to build safe AI by prioritizing profit and growth over safety. When the board actually tried to pull the lever, that accountability mechanism broke, and here we are. Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here . Not a subscriber? You can sign up here . Now, the question of AI safety is everywhere . This summer, AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic broke out of their testing environments and hacked real companies. The CEOs of these frontier labs have since called for a slowdown and asked Washington for help, but the White House’s answer was a voluntary accord — one that relies in part on the kind of board accountability that failed at OpenAI. Anthropic is also about to go public, which will put a whole new set of market pressures on OpenAI’s biggest competitor. Helen has seen up close what happens when safety commitments run headlong into commercial incentives. And as she put it to me, if our hopes for the future depend on any one person being trustworthy, we’re in big trouble. So we talked about what we might do instead: what the labs are actually trying to build, whether AI alignment is a problem that can be solved, and what a smarter approach to AI regulation might look like. That includes how to think about China, which is the issue that looms large in every policy conversation about AI right now — especially now after the Jensen Huang affair . Just for clarity, Helen and I talked before Nvidia opened its investigation and Jensen ultimately resigned, so you won’t hear us talk about that directly. Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube , where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday. Okay: Helen Toner, the executive director of CSET, on the future of AI safety. Here we go. This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity. Helen Toner, you’re the executive director for the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. Welcome to Decoder . Thanks so much. Great to be here. item.description:
Tariq is the Editor-in-Chief of Space.com based out of our New York City office and joined the team in 2001, first as an intern and staff writer, and later as an editor. He covers human spaceflight, exploration and space science, as well as skywatching and entertainment. He became Space.com's Managing Editor in 2009 and Editor-in-Chief in 2019. In October 2022, Tariq received the Harry Kolcum Award for excellence in space reporting from the National Space Club Florida Committee. In June 2025, the National Space Society awarded him the Space Pioneer Award for Excellence in Mass Media at the International Space Development Conference in Orlando, Florida.

Hailing from Stockton, California (where he attended the same high school as NASA astronaut Jose Hernandez), Tariq studied print journalism and astronomy at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles, earning a bachelor's degree in journalism in 1999 along with a minor in astronomy. He then served as a staff reporter for The Los Angeles Times covering education and city beats in La Habra and Fullerton in Orange County for the Our Times sections.

In 2000, Tariq became the city reporter for the Huntington Beach Independent, a weekly publication of the Los Angeles Times, covering local politics and events, crime, business and environmental issues. He left the Los Angeles Times in 2001 to study science journalism at New York University, where he earned a master's degree in 2002 from NYU's Science and Environmental Reporting Program (now the Science, Health and Environmental Reporting Program) under the direction of space reporter William Burrows.

Tariq first joined Space.com as an intern in September 2001 while also serving as a research assistant for nutrition writer Gary Taubes and writing freelance projects, where his work appeared in The Scientist and Laboratory Equipment Magazine. He became a full-time reporter covering spaceflight in 2004, with this first launch being NASA's STS-114 Return to Flight mission in July 2005.

Tariq is also an Eagle Scout (yes, he has the Space Exploration merit badge) and went to Space Camp four times as a kid and a fifth time as an adult. When not writing about space, you can find Tariq watching the latest Star Trek TV series, sci-fi movies and reading about hippos, his favorite animal. You can find Tariq at Space.com and as the co-host to the This Week In Space podcast with space historian Rod Pyle on the TWiT network. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
item.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: Mark Your Calendars! Lagos International Theatre Festival Returns to MUSON Centre This November
item.description: The Lagos International Theatre Festival ( LITF ) returns for its 2026 edition on November 14–15 at the MUSON Centre, Lagos, bringing together an exciting programme of theatre from Nigeria and around the world. The festival, which attracts more than 25,000 attendees across its programme days, has become one of the most anticipated events on Lagos’s cultural calendar. This year’s festival is themed “The Masks We Wear”, anchored by the statement “The Stage Is Everywhere.” The theme explores the different roles and identities people assume in everyday life, while inviting audiences to consider how theatre extends beyond the traditional stage. LITF 2026 brings an international dimension to Lagos, featuring artists and productions from Kenya, Canada and Brazil alongside a diverse Nigerian programme. An international highlight is LeRa Entertainments’ Under The Mango Tree from Canada, produced by Lennette Randall , with productions from Norway, Kenya and Brazil adding further cultural and theatrical perspectives. The Nigerian programme features productions from Lagos, Abuja, Enugu and Abeokuta, including Monkey Laundry , directed by Olarotimi Fakunle ; tHERapy , directed by Tosin Adeyemi ; What You Have Become , directed by Lanre Adediwura; and Behind Closed Doors , directed by Bolanle Austen-Peters. The festival will also spotlight emerging theatre makers through productions from Atlantic Hall, Evergreen College and Children’s International School, alongside professional and independent productions. The festival experience begins ahead of the main weekend with a series of events across Lagos. On November 9, Theatre Meets Food, hosted by Hilda Baci, will bring together artists, partners, cultural leaders and members of Lagos’s creative community for an evening of food, theatre and conversation. This will be followed by Embassy Nights on November 10 and 11, celebrating international cultural exchange among diplomatic representatives, artists and creative industry leaders. The programme culminates in an Opening Night Gala on November 13, ahead of the main festival weekend at MUSON Centre on November 14 and 15. LITF 2026 is supported by the Lagos State Government, LekOil, Pillar Oil, Afrexim and Amstel , alongside its growing network of international and cultural partners. Founder of LITF, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “The Masks We Wear is a theme that speaks to all of us. We all play different roles in our lives, and theatre allows us to examine those roles, question them, and perhaps see ourselves differently. This year, we are also reminding audiences that theatre is not confined to a theatre building. The stage is everywhere.” Festival Director, Vanessa Jev , said the diversity of voices at this year’s festival was particularly exciting, with Nigerian artists joining performers from Kenya, Canada and Brazil to create opportunities for audiences to experience different cultures and perspectives. Founded by Bolanle Austen-Peters, LITF celebrates theatre

item.title: Her Enterprise, Africa’s Advantage: HerSphere Global Summit 2026 Convenes Africa’s Foremost Women Leaders in Lagos
item.description: Africa’s economic story is increasingly being written by women. Across the continent, women own and operate a remarkable share of small and growing enterprises, sustain household and community economies, and drive innovation in sectors from finance and technology to the creative industries. Yet the gap between participation and power remains wide. Too many women-led businesses stay small, under-capitalised and absent from the rooms where markets, policy and capital are shaped. On Tuesday, 17 November 2026, the HerSphere Global Summit 2026 will gather a distinguished assembly of leaders at the Wole Soyinka Centre, Lagos, Nigeria, to confront that gap directly. Proceedings begin promptly at 9:00 a.m. A Theme That Demands Action This year’s theme, “ Her Enterprise, Africa Advantage: Moving Women-Led Businesses Beyond Participation to Economic Power,” reflects a deliberate shift in the conversation. The question is no longer whether women belong in Africa’s economy — that has long been settled. The question is how women-led enterprises can scale, command capital, influence policy and build institutions that endure. The summit is designed to move beyond inspiration to strategy: how women founders access growth finance, how they enter regional and global value chains, how public institutions and private capital can work together to back them, and how today’s enterprises become tomorrow’s market leaders. An Exceptional Line-Up of Voices HerSphere Global Summit 2026 brings together an exceptional roster of women who have shaped Nigeria’s and Africa’s judicial, public, financial, entrepreneurial and creative landscapes: • Hon. Justice Amina Adamu Augie (CFR) • Dolapo Osinbajo • Hannatu Musa Musawa • Godrey Ogbechie • Maisie Dunbar • Bolanle Austen-Peters • Uche Pedro • Jumoke Olaniyan • Monisola Olufunke Alabi • Brenda Nwagwu • Chioma Ude • Adesuwa Okunbo Rhodes • Ifeoma Uddoh • Temilade Aduroja • Lehle Balde • Arese Ugwu Together, they represent decades of leadership across law, public service, investment, media, entertainment, financial inclusion and enterprise building — and a shared conviction that Africa’s prosperity depends on the full economic power of its women. Backed by Institutions That Shape the Economy The summit is supported by a strong coalition of partners: the Lagos State Government, the Office of Sustainable Development Goals (Lagos Global), the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX), Delphino Entertainment, and SheMeansBusiness by BusinessDay. Their involvement underscores a growing recognition across government, capital markets and media that empowering women-led enterprise is not a social side-project — it is core economic strategy. item.title: 'Now everything changes': SpaceX catches Starship upper stage for 1st time ever (video)
item.description: null SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast today, his voice thick with emotion. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) The Ship catch occurred today at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time), roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. Many SpaceX employees went outside to watch the vehicle, known as Ship 42, descend through the clouds toward its Starbase launch tower, which the company calls "Mechazilla." And they got quite a show: Ship 42 nestled gently into Mechazilla's waiting arms, while "Baby Come Back" played over SpaceX's landing webcast. "This is so incredible to see," SpaceX's Jessie Anderson said during the livestream. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes." Why was this such a big deal? SpaceX had already caught Super Heavy — on three previous Starship test flights, in fact. But it had never tried before with Ship. The upper stage is a tougher target, for it flies higher, farther and faster than the booster. Indeed, on Flight 15, Ship 42 came all the way back down from orbit. Ship 42 comes in for its landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) While the double-catch attempt, and the chopsticks success with Ship, were Flight 15's main headlines, the mission had other objectives as well. One was getting Ship to orbit, which had happened on just one previous Starship launch — Flight 14 , which lifted off on Sept. 28. Ship deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) on Flight 14, and it did so again on Flight 15. These 52 spacecraft are the first members of a constellation that will eventually consist of 100,000 satellites , if all goes according to SpaceX's plan. item.title: James Webb telescope finds ice older than the star it orbits
item.description: Beta Pictoris is a young star, roughly 20 million years old, and located about 64 light-years away from Earth. It is surrounded by a vast disk of dust and rubble where planets are still forming—astronomers have already found three. In a new Science study, a team led by Sarah Betti, an astronomer at the Space Telescope Science Institute in Baltimore, used the James Webb Space Telescope to look for ice in this disk. Researchers found both water and carbon dioxide ice. The water ice is glassy rather than crystalline, and it is mixed with carbon dioxide in roughly the same proportions we see in comets of our own Solar System. This suggests ingredients necessary to form water-rich worlds might be common around young stars. The missing ice Beta Pictoris is one of the best studied stars in the sky. Its disk was among the first ever imaged, back in 1984, and we see it almost exactly edge-on, which makes it a natural laboratory for studying how planetary systems grow. It's what astronomers call a debris disk, where the dust is constantly replenished by collisions among comets and planetesimals, small bodies that are the building blocks of planets. The region produces about 90 percent of South Africa’s wine , but winemakers there are increasingly struggling with drought, excessive heat and erratic rainfall. Temperatures in the region have risen 1.5 to 2 times faster than the global average over the past five decades. And extreme storms have become more intense as climate variability increases. The late 2010s brought a significant challenge for winemakers, as three years of severe drought placed vineyards under intense stress and reduced grape production. As climate variability places increasing pressure on grape production, many wine producers are building on sustainability measures that have long been part of vineyard management. item.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
item.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? Then be sure to read our guide on everything you need to observe and photograph the planets of the solar system, along with our picks of the top telescopes , cameras and lenses for exploring the night sky in 2026. Editor's Note: If you would like to share your photos of Mars and Jupiter with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), comments, and your name and location to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: Microsoft's school email bill gives rivals something to smile about
item.description: The fallout from Microsoft's education price rises and service cuts continues as institutions weigh the prospect of bigger bills, and the Windows maker's rivals struggle not to pull "I told you so" faces. The main takeaways are that free student email and collaboration services are being retired, and storage entitlements are changing. These changes generally apply at institutions' first renewal or extension on or after January 1, 2028. Microsoft announced the new plans last week, and the UK's Department for Education described itself as "disappointed" at the news. As well it might be, although the UK government has rarely seen a deal from Microsoft that it didn't like . Or, for that matter, other US tech giants . Exactly how much educational institutions will have to spend remains unclear. Mary Jo Foley of Directions on Microsoft put indicative student pricing at $2 per year for Microsoft 365 Education A2, $4 for A3, and $6 for A5, with Teams adding another dollar annually. Faculty licenses cost considerably more, while the new A7 student tier jumps to $385 a year before Teams. Foley cautioned that these were approximate figures, with actual prices set by Microsoft's partners. The new no-cost student tier, Microsoft 365 Education A0, is a poor replacement for Office 365 A1: it excludes Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and Teams. Eligibility also requires full paid faculty coverage on A2 or higher and students who actively use Windows devices for education – potentially awkward for institutions running fleets of Chromebooks. A few dollars per student might not sound alarming. Multiply that across an institution, however, and something that used to be free becomes a recurring bill. Michael Meeks, CEO of Collabora Productivity, told The Register: "Free was the bait on the hook, and Microsoft spent years reeling in schools' email accounts, documents, identity management and classrooms onto its cloud." A poster on the edugeek.net forums commented: "This was always going to happen, I remember thinking this when we moved over to the MS free cloud solution. It will be free until they decide it isn't." The risk for Microsoft is that there are options. Meeks told us: "Schools now have a year to plan, and, in our experience with other large-scale educational projects, such as the University of Lille, that can be enough time to migrate properly." Other options include Nextcloud, which will be rolled out as part of Germany's Educational Cloud Infrastructure . Several Swiss universities also migrated to the service over an August weekend. According to Nextcloud, 39,500 students, teachers, and researchers, along with 585 terabytes of data, were shifted. Both Nextcloud and Collabora Productivity also highlight another factor that could drive educational institutions away from Microsoft: sovereignty. item.title: Big Tech takes a beating as online safety experts accuse companies of doing bare minimum
item.description: Technology companies are doing just enough to show a degree of compliance with the UK's Online Safety Act, but are failing to meet the needs of the individuals and young victims the legislation exists to protect, experts say. A panel of online safety pros assembled before Parliament's Communications and Digital Committee on Tuesday, taking aim at the likes of Google, Microsoft, Meta, and ByteDance for failing to act on important matters. Clare McGlynn, professor of law at Durham University and expert on violence against women and girls (VAWG), was especially critical of major search engine providers for their inconsistent downranking of harmful content search terms. "Rape porn," for example, is correctly downranked and no user sees any relevant links until the tenth page of results, although adjacent terms such as "unwilling porn" can be found as early as the third page, McGlynn said. "I just think if someone spent a little more time thinking 'I really want to minimize the risk of this material appearing,' I would take a systematic approach," she told the committee. "I would downrank 'unwilling' and 'unwanted,' and I would downrank 'asleep porn' as well… because it just means that it's easily findable. "So, they don't rank some of them, but just not systematically or wholly consistently." McGlynn went on to say that during her own research, "force porn" was rightly downranked heavily, although terms as similar as "forced porn" were not. "If you were trying to think of the words that would be similar to say rape, and rape porn is extreme porn and it's not supposed to be on those platforms anymore, you would think of words like unwilling and unwanted," she added. "And we know your algorithm would." Google inevitably took much of McGlynn's flak due to its dominance of the search engine market, although the professor said the same issues can be observed on Bing, too. Alexandra Whiston-Dew, partner at law firm Miscon de Raya, argued that search engines have such an important role in regulating the OSA, noting the limited resources at Ofcom's disposal. She said that more needs to be done from the tech side to ensure different parties in the chain of publication are detected early and downranked or blocked accordingly. There are publications, for example, that actively advertise themselves as websites that host illegal content, and these appear to be missing from the search engines' crosshairs. "So, they are spotlighting the fact that they are publishing illegal content, and this is going under the radar not only from the search engines but also the other platforms and the businesses in the chain of publication," said Whiston-Dew. "Also Ofcom needs to really pull all of their resources together and attack that receptacle of illegal content." Similarly, McGlynn raised the issue of porn sites continuing to host extreme porn, as they are legally allowed to do, to make it available to less regulated territories. item.title: New Scientist readers on how the magazine has shaped their lives
item.description: Have you been reading New Scientist since the start? Getty Images/Westend61 The first issue of New Scientist was published on 22 November 1956, and some of our readers have been with us since the very beginning. We asked subscribers, young and old, to tell us how they first encountered the magazine and how New Scientist has influenced their lives. The volume of responses and the gratitude expressed within them were quite overwhelming. Here are some of our favourites, featuring a spectacular maggot experiment, science-inspired poetry and even a match made on the short-lived New Scientist dating site. Huge thanks to everyone who wrote in. I was interested to see that New Scientist was launched “for all those men and women who are interested in scientific discovery and in its industrial, commercial and social consequences”. At the age of 13, I saved up a shilling from my Saturday morning “jobs” to purchase the first edition on 22 November 1956 and became one of those people interested in scientific discovery. Seventy years later, I remain a subscriber, after a scientific career that took me to many (if not, most!) countries in the world. New Scientist covered things like the opening of Jodrell Bank telescope in 1957. Since that was only about 50 miles (80 kilometres) away, it necessitated a bike ride to see what it really looked like! Peter Hall Advertisement I seem to have been reading New Scientist for the full 70! I do recall my encounter with the first edition: I was at Bec Grammar School in south London in a second-year physics class – it was 1956. The teacher, a genial boffin-type, announced the advent of the new publication and handed out copies – all I remember is its grey (or was it beige?) pages, which I read in a perfunctory way (I was only 12!) little thinking it would follow me through life and around the globe. Robyn Williams I was at Malvern College in England for my O level examinations from 1955 to 1958. My science master at Malvern had recognised my interest in science and technology and he bought the very first issue of New Scientist with his own money. At the next science class, he stood up in front of the whole class and waved the first issue, saying, “Young Inman, a new UK science and technology magazine has been published and here is the first issue for you.” I went on to reach 60 years as a member of the UK Institution of Civil Engineers. Peter Inman 1956 puts me back at school – Fettes College in Edinburgh. The school adopted New Scientist from its first edition and it was available in the library, where senior boys interested in science were recommended to read it. And so began a lifetime of New Scientist – I have been a regular for as long as I can remember and a subscriber for a very long time. I am very grateful to New Scientist for maintaining my interest in all the sciences and new developments, which I am sure has helped me to think laterally and to have a greater understanding of what makes everything tick. Frank Eva

The first stage ascended toward space flawlessly, releasing the upper stage above the Gulf of Mexico. item.title: SpaceX launches Starship on ambitious 22-hour Flight 15 test, but aborts booster 'chopsticks' catch (video)
item.description: null STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch. Following stage separation, Super Heavy reoriented for a planned return to Starbase as Ship powered its way toward low Earth orbit (LEO). SpaceX originally planned to catch Super Heavy with the Starbase launch tower's giant mechanical "chopstick" arms. But it wasn't to be: The company called off the catch attempt and brought the booster down for a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico about 6.5 minutes after launch, for reasons that were not immediately clear. A successful catch would have been a significant milestone for SpaceX and its efforts to design Starship as a fully and rapidly reusable launch vehicle. It would have been the first successful recovery of a Version 3 (V3) Super Heavy , which SpaceX began flying earlier this year. The company previously recovered three of its V1 Super Heavy vehicles and reused two of those in later flights. SpaceX's Starship megarocket launches on its 15th test flight from Starbase, Texas on Nov. 13, 2026. (Image credit: Future/Josh Dinner, Space.com) Ship goes to orbit Ship's Raptors continued to fire following stage separation, completing their first burn just after eight minutes into flight. All went according to plan after that for Ship as well: A second engine burn lasting about 20 seconds parked Ship in LEO at an altitude of around 170 miles (275 kilometers) at T+26 minutes and 10 seconds. "We’ve got a nominal orbit insertion, so Starship now in orbit around Earth for the second time ever," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during today's Flight 15 launch webcast. "That’s a really great moment." Ship first reached orbit on Flight 14 , which launched on Sept. 28. Ship carried 26 of SpaceX's Starlink V3 spacecraft, which were deployed into LEO on schedule today over a 42-minute span starting 35 minutes after launch. The upgraded wireless internet satellites are the second V3 batch to reach orbit, after a set of 26 that were delivered on Flight 14 . V3s are significantly more powerful than SpaceX's V2 Starlinks, which currently number more than 11,000 in LEO. The addition of this new set of V3s will add a terabit of data capacity to the constellation, according to SpaceX's Flight 15 mission outline . That's equivalent to the
